📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, I have to admit that when I first saw the Fangchengbao Tai 9 stow its steering wheel away on social media, I assumed that it was AI. It wasn't. This BYD brand's latest SUV can indeed retract its steering wheel right into the dashboard. However, it’s not quite used for the reason you’d think.

The Tai 9 is a six-seat, plug-in hybrid SUV about the same size as the Cadillac Escalade IQ, and it sits at the top of the Fangchengbao range. BYD’s Chinese-market brand and naming structure can be confusing, but in essence, Fangchengbao is one of BYD's premium brands.

Power comes from two electric motors that produce 536 horsepower at peak, while a 1.5-liter turbocharged engine is responsible for any combustion-powered driving. The Tai 9 has a 66.5 kWh battery that is capable of BYD’s flash charging technology. The brand claims it can sprint from 10% to 97% in nine minutes.

In a recent development, those are all very compelling specs, but the most interesting part of the Tai 9 is the top-of-the-line Foldable Smart Cabin trim. Since the Tai 9 uses a steer-by-wire system, the steering wheel can fold up and stow itself in the dashboard. BYD says that takes about 10 seconds.

However, this isn’t for any sort of autonomous driving. China’s autonomous driving rules are strict, and no automaker in the country has approval for commercially sold eyes-off, hands-off driver assist features. Instead, the folding steering wheel is primarily for comfort and space, specifically when the car is stationary. Photos of the feature in action show that stowing away the steering wheel makes extra room for a little table setup.

This isn’t entirely unprecedented. The upcoming trend in China is for large SUVs to be third spaces where buyers can comfortably hang out, even when they aren't driving. The Tai 9’s Nappa leather, comfy seats, and second-row folding screen are meant to make it a calming, relaxing space to spend time. It's similar in concept to what we’ve seen on the Zeekr Mix and SkyNomad N90 Studio.

Still, despite the Tai 9’s folding steering wheel not being for self-driving, I wouldn’t be surprised if it does show up in cars for that reason someday, as manufacturers strive to make cars that can truly drive themselves.

A car with no steering wheel at all might feel risky and uncomfortable to some car buyers, especially if it's like Tesla’s Cybercab, which can’t be driven manually at all above low speeds. Yet, if there were a backup to take control, I could see that putting some minds at ease.

Recent findings suggest that the Fangchengbao Tai 9 is on sale in China for about $42,000. The top-of-the-line model with the foldable steering wheel is about $49,500.

BYD is preparing to launch a latest flagship MPV soon after previewing the large people mover for the first time.

We knew it was coming soon after images of the camouflaged multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) began flooding the internet last month.

Zhang Zhuo, general manager of BYD’s Ocean sales division, confirmed the new flagship MPV is coming soon.

“A newly introduced creation for the times, born for the family,” Zhuo remarked after posting a preview of it for the first time on his Weibo account on Friday.

It has been revealed that the fresh flagship Ocean MPV is “coming soon,” according to Zhuo, but he didn’t reveal a specific debut date. He previously said the tech giant expects to launch its first MPV under the Ocean lineup by the end of 2026, so local reports suggest it will make an official debut next week at the 2026 Guangzhou Auto show, which kicks off on November 27.

Although it’s blurred, the preview highlights a similar shape and size to the recent spy images, with a roof-mounted LiDAR and traditional pull-style door handles.

It doesn’t appear to look much like the futuristic Ocean-V concept BYD unveiled at the 2026 Beijing Auto Show earlier this year, a preview of its first MPV under the Ocean series.

According to recent reports, the concept featured a sliding center display screen and two different modes: Camping and Movie. In camping mode, the seats either fold flat to create a bed or swivel to face each other.

In Movie mode, the vehicle transforms into a private mobile theater with a large display screen that flips out of the dashboard.

While it may not have some of the more extravagant elements from the concept, the Ocean MPV is expected to be “flagship-worthy,” if you will, with BYD’s latest tech and other premium features like zero-gravity seats and plenty of digital screens.

The Ocean-V’s innovations “will gradually make their way into mass-production vehicles,” BYD mentioned earlier this year.

BYD has yet to announce any details, but the flagship Ocean MPV is expected to be about the size of the Xia, a large plug-in hybrid minivan sold under its Dynasty lineup.

The BYD Xia measures 5,145 mm long, 1,970 mm wide, and 1,805 mm tall, with a 3,045 mm wheelbase.

Like the Xia, the Ocean MPV is expected to use BYD’s latest-generation DM-i plug-in hybrid system with a 1.5L engine and a 200 kW electric motor.

The Xia starts at 249,800 yuan ($37,500) in China. It’s available with two BYD Blade LFP battery packs: 20.4 kWh and 36.6 kWh, providing pure electric CLTC ranges of 100 km (62 miles) and 218 km (135 miles). On a full tank of gas and full charge, the plug-in people mover offers a combined CLTC range of 1,163 km (722 miles).

It has been revealed that BYD also sells the flagship Denza D9 MPV under its luxury sub-brand. With the Denza D9 starting above 300,000 yuan and the Xia at around 250,000 yuan, the Ocean MPV is expected to fill the gap.

Zhuo said to stay tuned for more coming soon, so check back for updates.

Electric Vans — Are They The Final EV Frontier? Kia PV5.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that we took a trip to see the Kia PV5 electric van.
  • Inspired by a comment in the Electric Vehicle Council report about electric vans, Majella and I decided to have a short visit to a group of dealerships under the Norris Motors banner.
  • Julie Delvecchio, the CEO of EVC, calls the lack of affordable electric vans in Australia “the single biggest unclaimed opportunity left.” We think that is about to change.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that we took a trip to see the Kia PV5 electric van. Our brief takeaway: “Kool like a Kia.” Should keep the bean counters happy.

Inspired by a comment in the Electric Vehicle Council report about electric vans, Majella and I decided to have a short visit to a group of dealerships under the Norris Motors banner. We hoped to check out the LDV eDeliver 5 van, touted as selling for under AU$50,000. However, there was no stock to view and we ended up chatting to the dealer and then moving on to the MG U9 BEV ute. You can read about it here. And then we found the Kia PV5 delivery van.

Julie Delvecchio, the CEO of EVC, calls the lack of affordable electric vans in Australia “the single biggest unclaimed opportunity left.” We think that is about to change. Since its launch in May, 496 PV5 have sold in Australia.

Sources indicate that the Kia PV5 reminded me a lot of the Renault Kangoo in both size and shape, and it is able to carry about the same payload. And the front looked like the BMW i3. The one we looked at had been sold and was awaiting a fitout as a camper van. The Norris Group Kia specialist was generous with his time and the information he shared. He has been selling the Kia EV5 for the past 5 months and delivered 5 of the vans. He sold his first one within a week of its arrival on the lot — to Ray, a driver working for Amazon.

According to recent reports, ray appreciated the 390 km range. My friendly sales rep tells me that this will be increased in 2027 models to 420 km. Ray was getting out of diesel and most of his questions were around charging and regen braking. Most of his trips were around the burbs and he was not intending to take the van on the highway. The Kia PV5 is a workhorse, with a passenger car feel and level of comfort. It even has electric lumbar support for the driver — great when you are spending so much time in the van delivering parcels in the lead-up to Christmas. It certainly has a lot more tech than the diesel he was trading in.

In fact, he was “blown away” by the standard features — the 360-degree camera, for example. “Vans are not known for their visibility.” On his return to the dealership for his first service, he commented on the smoothness of the torque: “It has no challenges going uphill.” He reported that the van felt “well planted on the road.” Ray has gotten used to trickle charging at home and has lost his range anxiety. Like most new EV drivers, once he started living and working with the vehicle, his fears vanished. The PV5 supports fast charging also for when Ray needs a boost on the road.

In a recent development, but what about that all-crucial question of cost? Can we make the bean counters happy? The Kia PV5 retails for AU$56,000 (before on-road costs), which is about the same price as comparable diesel vans like the Ford Transit and the Toyota HiAce. Add to that the savings on fuel, the peace of mind from fuel security, and the reduced servicing and it is easy to build a business case for the Kia PV5 — cost per parcel delivery. The PV5 even comes with vehicle to load.

And it isn’t made in China! Can the PV5 replace Toyota’s HiAce? Find the answer in this video. The reviewer points out many features that make the PV5 an attractive option: the charge port is on the front. The van has lots of nooks and crannies for storage. She measures storage by capacity to fit in bottles of wine — for example, two in the glove box. There is a step provided to alight the van, aided by grab handles. More storage space is provided above the steering wheel, including a nifty phone slot. There are customizable buttons on the steering wheel to create shortcuts; for example, to the air conditioning settings. A wireless phone charger is nestled near the dash. The glovebox contains the V2L adaptor supplied with the van.

Industry observers note that the fact that the van reverts to the lowest regen setting every time you restart the car is a little niggle. That, and there is no frunk — reducing the reviewer’s all-important need for wine storage. Full specs can be found here. Kia even gives you helpful advice on how to apply for electric vehicle subsidies (last page, bottom right). One of the pictures that caught my eye demonstrates the PV5 as a flatbed truck.

The PV5 was recently named 2026 International Van of the Year. It measures 4695mm long, 2255mm wide, and 1899mm tall on a 2995mm wheelbase. Range is stated as 416 km, but will of course vary with driving style and load. The battery is a 71.2kWh nickel cobalt manganese (NCM) lithium-ion battery. Kia offers a 165,000 km warranty on the battery. The van is front-wheel drive.

The PV5 has over 4 cubic metres of cargo capacity, double both that of the ID Buzz and the Tesla Model Y. Space enough for two euro pallets. There are multiple access points, with sliding doors on both sides and barn doors in the rear. The rear barn doors open to 180 degrees, and a low 419mm load height improves accessibility.

It has been revealed that goods being shipped are protected by padding on the rear doors and insides of the back. The PV5 can carry up to 740 kg. Tiedowns on the floor of the rear of the van help to secure cargo. There is also a power point in the back of the van. Perhaps a tradie can recharge their tools on site. No frunk for wine.

From the spec sheet: “Standard driver assist features include blind-spot collision avoidance, navigation-based adaptive cruise control, lane-keep assist, lane centring with hands-on detection, and parking collision avoidance assist.”.

A launch in the USA is financially difficult because of the 25% “chicken tax.” Kia builds the PV5 in South Korea and classifies it as a commercial vehicle, and it faces a 25% US import tariff on light trucks and commercial vans.

Recent findings suggest that sadly, the Kia PV5 doesn’t come in red, but only in white, grey and black. Most companies may take up the option of wrapping the van in their own livery. Overall, we were impressed with Kia PV5 and look forward to seeing more of them on the road throughout the suburbs as Australian delivery drivers move towards a bright electric future.

Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cleantechnica

Industry News: Sierra Club Submits Comments Urging SEC to Preserve Shareholder Rights & Climate Accountability

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (519 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • — On Thursday, Sierra Club submitted two comment letters opposing the Securities and Exchange Commission’s (SEC) proposal to rescind Rule 14a-8, which allows shareholders to put proposals addressing climate risks and other corporate complications before fellow investors for a vote, and amend Rule 14a-4(c), which governs how companies may exercise discretionary voting authority over shareholder proposals.
  • Together the submissions urge the SEC to withdraw its proposed changes and preserve investors’ ability to raise concerns directly with corporate management and press companies to address material risks, including climate-related risks, that can affect their long-term financial interests.
  • Jessye Waxman, Campaign Advisor on Sierra Club’s Sustainable Finance Campaign, released the following statement:.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

WASHINGTON, D.C. — On Thursday, Sierra Club submitted two comment letters opposing the Securities and Exchange Commission’s (SEC) proposal to rescind Rule 14a-8, which allows shareholders to put proposals addressing climate risks and other corporate complications before fellow investors for a vote, and amend Rule 14a-4(c), which governs how companies may exercise discretionary voting authority over shareholder proposals. The Sierra Club submitted both a technical comment and a grassroots comment, reflecting concerns from over 1,100 of its members and supporters.

Together the submissions urge the SEC to withdraw its proposed changes and preserve investors’ ability to raise concerns directly with corporate management and press companies to address material risks, including climate-related risks, that can affect their long-term financial interests.

Jessye Waxman, Campaign Advisor on Sierra Club’s Sustainable Finance Campaign, released the following statement:.

Recent findings suggest that “Climate change and other systemic risks have real consequences for companies, investors, and the broader economy. Shareholder proposals give investors an key way to bring those risks to management’s attention, push for meaningful action, and hold companies accountable when they fail to act. The SEC’s proposals would weaken those tools, making it harder for investors to protect their long-term financial interests and leaving corporate management with less accountability for the risks its decisions create. The SEC’s proposals would shield corporate management from meaningful shareholder scrutiny, while undermining the very investor protections the Commission is charged with upholding.”.

It has been revealed that rule 14a-8 establishes when public companies must include qualifying shareholder proposals in the materials they send investors ahead of shareholder meetings. The SEC’s proposed repeal would leave decisions about shareholder proposals to state law and individual companies’ governing documents, eliminating a federal framework that investors have used for more than 80 years.

It has been revealed that sierra Club’s technical comments explain that material risks, like climate change, can both have significant financial consequences for companies and create systemic financial risks that extend across investment portfolios and the broader economy. Shareholder proposals give investors a way to bring these concerns to manufacturer leadership and fellow shareholders, including by surfacing risks that management may overlook or have limited incentives to address. The letter emphasizes that, for decades, this process has served the broader market by helping investors collectively identify and address financially material risks.

The letter warns that replacing a consistent federal framework with varying state laws and corporate bylaws could make shareholder engagement less predictable and push disputes over proposals into costly litigation. It points to the increase in shareholder lawsuits challenging proposal exclusions during the 2026 proxy season as an indication that disputes do not disappear when the SEC steps back from administering the process; instead, they can shift to more costly and uncertain avenues.

According to recent reports, the submission also opposes proposed amendments to Rule 14a-4(c), which would expand company management’s discretionary authority to vote shareholders’ proxies on proposals excluded from company proxy materials, unless shareholders affirmatively opt out. Sierra Club’s letter warns that these changes could allow management to vote on proposals that investors have not had an adequate opportunity to evaluate.

#564. Pacific Power Begins Latest Customer Protections Against Data Centers

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (740 w)
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Cleantechnica

Pacific Power Begins Latest Customer Protections Against Data Centers

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (740 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Regulators approve fresh agreement to ensure data centers pay for their own energy costs.
  • Sources indicate that SALEM, Oregon — The Oregon Public Utility Commission has approved an agreement between advocates and Pacific Power.
  • 1, 2027, upcoming Pacific Power data centers will be held responsible for their own energy costs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Regulators approve fresh agreement to ensure data centers pay for their own energy costs.

Sources indicate that SALEM, Oregon — The Oregon Public Utility Commission has approved an agreement between advocates and Pacific Power. Now, Pacific Power customers have a strong suite of protections against data centers’ impact on Oregonians’ energy bills.

Starting Jan. 1, 2027, upcoming Pacific Power data centers will be held responsible for their own energy costs. These new rules will only apply to future data centers and existing ones making significant investments, which regulators identified as the most pressing challenge to address. Right now, the utility has very few existing data centers on its system.

“With a long line of data centers waiting at Pacific Power’s door, I’m confident that we have the right protections at the right time,” said Bob Jenks, Executive Director of Oregon Citizens’ Utility Board. “We were able to stop more extreme impacts on power bills just in time.”.

Industry observers note that data centers over 100 MW will also have to pay a small surcharge to fund energy efficiency upgrades for low-income households. This includes funding for deep home retrofits, lowering energy use across the grid while saving customers on monthly bills.

“Many of the households we serve are already struggling to afford their energy bills and risk having their utilities shut off. Data centers will help fund weatherization, energy efficiency upgrades, and the critical home repairs that often prevent our clients from accessing these improvements in the first place,” mentioned Charity Fain, Executive Director of Community Energy Project. “Requiring data centers to cover the costs of the energy infrastructure they need, rather than passing those costs on to residential customers, is an notable protection for low-income households, seniors, and people with disabilities.”.

Recent findings suggest that under this order, if there is a power emergency, Pacific Power can prioritize critical energy use for other customers, like renters and homeowners, by curtailing service to data centers. Increased electric demand by data centers strains the grid and increases the potential for blackouts during heat waves or hard freezes.

Sources indicate that “This is a major win that puts Oregon at the forefront of managing data center growth the right way,” noted Joshua Basofin, Oregon Clean Energy Program Director at Climate Solutions. “It protects Oregonians from rising costs and strengthens grid resilience. Data centers should not harm our ability to access essential electricity to power our lives and keep us safe all year.”.

Regulators also ruled that fresh data centers can only be connected to Pacific Power’s grid if there is enough emissions-free electricity available to serve them. Under HB 2021, Pacific Power is required by law to serve all customers with 100% emissions-free electricity by 2040. This new rule will help manage costs for other customers outside of data centers during the transition to clean energy.

Sources indicate that “We have long known that clean energy is the most affordable form of energy,” said Ben Brint, Senior Climate Program Director at Oregon Environmental Council. “This ruling is a win for data center accountability, and for Oregonians across the state — especially frontline communities already bearing the brunt of climate impacts and rising energy costs. It will save ratepayers money in the short and long run, allocating costs appropriately while advancing Oregon’s 100% clean energy goals.”.

This change also comes at a time when many Oregonians are calling for broader changes to how the state handles data centers. Impacts on data centers are poised to be an issue again at the Oregon State Legislature in 2027.

“The POWER Act demonstrated the people’s power to fight back against the rising energy rates and ecosystem harms that large data centers inflict,” noted Emily Bowes, Policy Strategist & Acting Director at Sierra Club Oregon. “In 2027, alongside newly introduced and returning climate champions, we will continue to fight for a clean energy transition in Salem and statewide.”.

Industry observers note that in 2025, the Oregon Legislature passed the POWER Act to help utilities rein in data centers’ added costs to Oregonians’ energy bills. Last fall, Portland General Electric began the work to roll out this new law in practice. In January, Pacific Power started a similar process for its customers. The next step is to address the few existing data centers on Pacific Power’s system, starting as early as summer 2027. It is unclear if the final phase will include rate adjustments.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • More so than any of its predecessors, "Grand Theft Auto 6" leans heavily into realism.
  • To be fair to "Grand Theft Auto 6," it does remember that it is an action/adventure game and not the next coming of "Car Mechanic Simulator." For instance, stops to get your car fixed are generally pretty brief.
  • Recent findings suggest that still, the game does feature four different ways to get your car fixed: Pay 'N' Spray shops, mod shops, gas stations, and a guy named Joey who can be called upon to do repairs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

More so than any of its predecessors, "Grand Theft Auto 6" leans heavily into realism. You can't just carry your entire arsenal on you anymore — instead, you must rely on a few guns on your person and a stash in your trunk. Building off that simulated realism, the game now puts a greater emphasis on the exciting world of vehicle maintenance directly into the gameplay. There will be times when you have to get your car repaired, repainted, or refueled. Who knows — maybe "Grand Theft Auto 7" will go one step further by including a mission called "Doing Taxes.".

To be fair to "Grand Theft Auto 6," it does remember that it is an action/adventure game and not the next coming of "Car Mechanic Simulator." For instance, stops to get your car fixed are generally pretty brief. That way, you can get right back to running heists and stealing a car that looks a lot like a Pontiac Trans Am out of a police impound lot.

Recent findings suggest that still, the game does feature four different ways to get your car fixed: Pay 'N' Spray shops, mod shops, gas stations, and a guy named Joey who can be called upon to do repairs. Gas stations are limited in the repairs they can do and are more expensive than other repair shops — there's that realism again. For more extensive repairs, you'll need to stop at one of the other shops or call Joey.

According to recent reports, missions can be pretty rough on your vehicles, especially when you're trying to get away from the cops. Your car can get engine damage or cosmetic damage, and fixing it can be important to the gameplay. One of the early missions, "Just a Scratch," will actually make you take your vehicle into Coastal Auto Care to get fixed. That's where you meet Joey.

Industry observers note that throughout the game, there is an engine condition indicator that goes from green to orange to red. It ends off at red with an "X" in the middle, indicating that the engine is dead. Green indicates the engine is in good shape, orange means there is moderate damage, and red indicates critical damage. An engine that is not in good shape can affect how the car performs, which is not something you want to deal with as your wanted level increases.

And don't forget to fuel up, as each car has a working fuel gauge. But don't worry, because you won't have to stop for gas too often; apparently "Grand Theft Auto 6" cars get pretty great gas mileage. EVs are also a part of the universe, which means you'll have to stop for a charge every so often if you grab one.

Recent findings suggest that the cars in "Grand Theft Auto 6" are not indestructible, but they can keep running even after getting pretty banged up. So, why bother to fix body damage? You don't want the NPCs to point and laugh at your car, do you? Even if you aren't worried about the opinions of Vice City pedestrians, the condition of your car's body can affect gameplay as well. Want to sell that hot car that you just stole? Well, just like in real life, damage to the body of the car can affect how much it sells for.

Then there's the matter of getting away from the cops after stealing a car. They will often have the car's description, including its color. There are even Flock-like cameras in GTA 6 that can track your movements. Repainting it another color, even when the body is in good shape, can help hide it from the police. It's like a wardrobe change, but for your vehicle. Pay 'N' Spray is the place to go for a quick paint job, while mod shops will be able to make more extensive changes to your car.

Industry observers note that overall, it seems like Rockstar has found a nice balance between the realities of car ownership and the escapist fantasy that the Grand Theft Auto series has always embodied. We'll just have to wait and see if "Car Mechanic Simulator 2027" will be adding heists.

The Volkswagen ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Is A Two-Seat Track-Ready EV

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (875 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Insideevs

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Volkswagen may not be in the best place right now, but that’s not stopping it from spending big money to celebrate the 50th anniversary of the legendary GTI badge.
  • Recent findings suggest that the striking electric race car comes after the production-ready ID.
  • According to recent reports, that stated, making the latest one-off wasn’t easy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Volkswagen may not be in the best place right now, but that’s not stopping it from spending big money to celebrate the 50th anniversary of the legendary GTI badge. The latest showpiece is the Volkswagen ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept, a one-off electric hatchback built for the track that sheds a set of doors and borrows the electric motor from its bigger brothers.

Recent findings suggest that the striking electric race car comes after the production-ready ID. Polo GTI and the upcoming ID.3 GTI, and its purpose is to show what the German brand can do with its modular MEB+ platform. In fact, Volkswagen is calling itself the “master of modular platforms,” proudly saying that the same architecture that underpins the bog-standard ID. Polo is capable of impressive extremes, from the ultra-efficient Mission Efficiency to the performance-oriented GTI Clubsport EV.

According to recent reports, that stated, making the latest one-off wasn’t easy. Engineers had to take an APP550 electric motor, which was originally designed for rear-wheel-drive models like the ID.7 and ID. Tiguan, and adapt it for the ID. Polo chassis, which is front-wheel-drive.

To fit the larger drive unit in the small hatchback, the whole front section of the car had to be modified, which meant designing and building an entirely new subframe. The longitudinal chassis members, stabilizer bar, several mounting points, and various chassis components also had to be redesigned to make the taller APP550 drive unit fit under the hood.

What’s more, the high-voltage charger, air conditioning compressor, thermal management module, and the water pump had to be relocated. Designers and engineers worked together to develop special holders, adapters, and mounting concepts to make it all work.

The ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept’s powertrain makes 362 horsepower and 406 pound-feet (550 Newton-meters) of torque, making it the most powerful electric Polo ever made. Compared to the road-going ID. Polo GTI, it makes 139 more horsepower and 192 more pound-feet of torque.

It has been revealed that yet, the car is still front-wheel drive. And if you’ve driven a relatively torquey EV with FWD, you know that transferring everything that an electric drive unit can give to the front wheels can prove difficult. But Volkswagen has that covered with an electronic front differential lock that uses a multiplate clutch. With it, the car can transfer power to both wheels if one of them starts to lose traction.

Sources indicate that all of that power and torque give the electric track car a zero-to-62 miles per hour (0-100 kilometers per hour) sprint time of 4.7 seconds and a 149 miles pr hour (240 kilometers per hour) top speed. To enable this level of performance, the 52-kilowatt-hour battery, which is the same as in the production ID. Polo GTI, was tweaked to allow for a higher power output of up to 290 kW, as well as longer discharge periods at high outputs.

Recent findings suggest that hooked to a DC fast charger, the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept can take up to 105 kW, just like the regular ID. Polo GTI, which can go from 10% to 80% in 24 minutes.

Industry observers note that the extra power and torque go hand in hand with plenty of changes to the body and underneath it. The one-off EV is 100 millimeters (3.9 inches) wider than the production model and sits 30 mm (1.1 in) lower than the standard ID. Polo. The same adaptive suspension as the production vehicle is used, but its setup is adjusted for track use.

In a recent development, the electric Clubsport Concept has just two doors instead of the regular ID. Polo’s four, and features a pretty aggressive body kit with wide wheel arches, functional air ducts, and a huge rear wing. GTI badges and red accents are everywhere, including in the interior, where the central touchscreen no longer acts as the infotainment center. In fact, the concept doesn’t have an infotainment system, as the central screen handles driving settings exclusively.

Bright red five-point harnesses protect the driver and front passenger sitting in Recaro racing bucket seats, while a red rollover bar has replaced the rear seats and cargo area.

Recent findings suggest that the Volkswagen ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept is not yet intended for production, but the German automaker hasn’t ruled out the option entirely, saying that it has always associated the development of concept vehicles “with the theoretical option of turning a one-off into a new production derivative.”.

The track-focused EV will make its first live appearance at the Essen Motor Show in Germany, which runs from November 27 through December 6.

AGCO Celebrates Construction Milestone at Olmedo Solar Project in Spain

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that OLMEDO, Spain, Nov.
  • Sources indicate that the milestone follows AGCO’s September 2025 announcement of its 10-year VPPA with BRUC.
  • “Project Olmedo will give AGCO long-term price certainty for the majority of the electricity certificate cost in Europe,” said Tim Millwood, Senior Vice President, Chief Supply Chain Officer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that OLMEDO, Spain, Nov. 19, 2026 — AGCO (NYSE: AGCO) today declared that Project Olmedo, the solar installation at the center of its first Virtual Power Purchase Agreement (VPPA), has completed construction and commissioning and is expected to begin delivering renewable electricity to the Spanish power grid in the coming months, pending final regulatory approvals. BRUC, one of the largest renewable energy groups in Spain, built the upcoming solar installation in the northwest province of Valladolid.

Sources indicate that the milestone follows AGCO’s September 2025 announcement of its 10-year VPPA with BRUC. The installation’s two solar projects, Los Silos and El Granero, span approximately 300 hectares (741 acres) and hold approximately 150,000 solar panels. AGCO’s portion of the installation’s annual production is expected to be approximately 150 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of renewable electricity a year, equivalent to the annual electricity consumption of approximately 40,000 European households, based on Eurostat data.

“Project Olmedo will give AGCO long-term price certainty for the majority of the electricity certificate cost in Europe,” said Tim Millwood, Senior Vice President, Chief Supply Chain Officer. “In volatile energy markets, securing that stability for 10 years strengthens the resilience of our supply chain while supporting new renewable generation.”.

Industry observers note that A VPPA lets a firm support fresh renewable energy projects without taking direct delivery of the electricity they generate. Because AGCO’s agreement supported the construction of a brand-new installation, it will add new renewable capacity to the grid rather than drawing on existing sources, a principle known as additionality. The agreement also helps reduce AGCO’s Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions from purchased electricity in its Europe/Middle East (EME) region and supports its commitment to reduce absolute Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 55% by 2033 from a 2022 baseline.

“Additionality is what makes this agreement truly meaningful,” mentioned Roger Batkin, Senior Vice President, Corporate Affairs, General Counsel & Corporate Secretary. “We did not simply buy renewable electricity that already existed; we supported the construction of a brand-new renewable solar project. Accomplishing this project required over two years of involvement from many teams, functions, and areas of expertise across AGCO, along with technical advisory support from Schneider Electric and a strong partnership with BRUC.”.

Reflecting AGCO’s Farmer-First strategy, Project Olmedo supports local farmers to further diversify their land use by leasing land for the project while maintaining the option for livestock to graze among the panels, maintaining the vegetation in place of machinery.

Industry observers note that AGCO and BRUC leaders, joined by local community representatives José Emilio Escudero García, Mayor of Bocigas, and Ursino Vara Pérez, Mayor of Almenara de Adaja, marked the milestone with a ribbon-cutting ceremony at the site in November. Additional drone footage from Project Olmedo and the ribbon-cutting event are available on AGCO’s YouTube page.

For more details on AGCO’s sustainability initiatives, visit the manufacturer’s sustainability webpage and read the 2025 Sustainability Report. For more information about BRUC, visit the company’s website at brucenergy.com.

According to recent reports, AGCO (NYSE: AGCO) is a global leader in agricultural machinery and precision agriculture technologies. Driven by a Farmer-First strategy, AGCO delivers value through its differentiated leading brands, Fendt™, Massey Ferguson™, PTx™ and Valtra™. AGCO’s high-performance equipment and smart farming solutions, including brand-agnostic retrofit technologies and autonomous offerings, empower farmers to drive productivity while sustainably feeding the world. For more information, visit www.agcocorp.com.

At $4,000, Is This 2002 Honda CR-V EX AWD A Keeper?

  • One of the coolest parts of the Mission Impossible franchise—both the '60s TV series and more recent movies—is the conceit where an agent masks up to imitate a target.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A lower-mileage engine and rare five-speed manual make the 241,000 miles on today's Nice Price or No Dice CR-V less of a concern. Let's see if this utilitarian compact crossover's price proves a hurdle we can't get past.

One of the coolest parts of the Mission Impossible franchise—both the '60s TV series and more recent movies—is the conceit where an agent masks up to imitate a target. The chef's kiss is seeing the secret agent reach under their collar to yank off the duplicative mask, thus revealing their true identity—typically Tom Cruise.

We had a similar experience on Thursday with the 1987 Fiero-based Corson, which was trying—somewhat successfully from a few angles, some might argue—to look like a Ferrari 512 BBi. At $26,000, there was no fooling our jaded eyes, however, causing the Corson Fiero to go up in flames in a massive 90% 'No Dice' loss.

Sources indicate that because yesterday's candidate was excessive in its owner's aspirations and the fakery it would take to make those aspirations a reality, it might be a nice contrast today to go with a candidate that is more sensible and grounded. That's not to say that this 2002 Honda CR-V EX AWD is dull as dishwater. How could it be with all those letters in its name? The CR-V has been Honda's best-selling vehicle here in the U.S. since 2017, and according to the firm's press site, "America's CUV best-selling since its U.S. launch in 1997." By the way, that's "Crossover Utility Vehicle" to you and me.

Loosely based on the Civic's platform and mechanicals, the first-generation CR-V offered a tall wagon experience in a manageable size and with reasonable fuel economy. That first generation also had an externally mounted spare tire and could have originally come with a clever, pull-out folding-leg table in the load area.

It has been revealed that okay, so far, that, save for the spare and the table, could describe just about any of the CR-V's competitors from when it was newly introduced or even clogging showrooms today. So what makes this particular car interesting?

It has been revealed that this 2002 edition was originally spec'd with a five-speed manual transmission and Honda's "Real Time" AWD behind its 2.4-liter, 160 horsepower VTEC four. That's a very rare combo on this car. According to the ad, that drivetrain has racked up a notable 241,000 miles under this CR-V's tires.

Not everything has made it that far, as the ad also touts an engine replacement in 2024 with a 60K unit and new gearbox synchros installed at some point. This year, it got a new catalytic converter, so smogging the car shouldn't be an issue. No mention is made about the clutch, but who does an engine swap or gearbox work without replacing the clutch? Reassuringly, the seller does claim that "everything works great," including the A/C, which they say blows cold.

Despite the miles and age, this CR-V still looks to have plenty of fight left in it. That's not to say it doesn't have a couple of battle scars. It does, after all, live in Los Angeles. Honda was very generous with the black plastic moldings on these first-gen cars, and they tend to turn gray and develop swirlies over time. A good plastic protector helps a lot, and this car seems to have been wiped down before its photo shoot. Missing on the exterior are the chrome inlay for the Honda badge in the grille and a chunk of the plastic fender arch over the left-rear wheel. Taking its place, and calling even more attention to its absence, is a sizable dent just behind the fuel filler door. Other than that, and some minor yellowing of the headlamp covers, the exterior looks to be in solid shape.

The cabin tells a similar story, and it happily features patterned mouse-fur upholstery rather than less durable leather. Seat controls are manual, but offer a number of knobs and levers to help occupants get comfortable. The rear bench includes a center fold-out armrest with similar intent. Sadly, the pull-out table appears to have gone missing, or was never there in the first place.

Recent findings suggest that in the film "Invasion of the Body Snatchers" (any of them, take your pick), the heroes fight an overwhelming effort by the titular invaders to assimilate them into a hive-mind collective. I'm not suggesting any of us get sucked into the CUV or Crossover cult, but if we were, this CR-V might prove a reasonable point of entry, given its specs. The question is: would it be worth $4,000 to do so?

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that GM says the pilot participants will be its first EV drivers in California to export power from their cars to their homes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, GM Energy and WeaveGrid are launching a vehicle-to-grid (V2G) pilot that will let select Southern California Edison (SCE) customers send electricity from their EV batteries back to the grid. Eligible drivers could get more than $16,000 in help with equipment and installation, and earn money when the grid needs their power.

Sources indicate that GM says the pilot participants will be its first EV drivers in California to export power from their cars to their homes. Through the California Energy Commission, eligible customers in SCE’s Emergency Load Reduction Program can get up to $8,000 toward a GM Energy V2H system and up to $8,099 toward eligible installation costs, including connecting the system to the grid.

Chevy, GMC, and Cadillac EV drivers can use time-of-use energy management to take advantage of lower rates and may be paid for participating in eligible demand-response events. How much they save or earn depends on their rate blueprint, electricity use, and participation.

GM already offers managed charging through 13 utilities, and each program varies by utility.

According to recent reports, an EV battery stores direct current (DC), and your house and the grid use alternating current (AC). GM’s current home backup system uses a wall-mounted inverter to convert the power. With AC bidirectional charging, the car’s onboard inverter does the job. Moving that work into the car could make the equipment on your garage wall simpler and cheaper to install.

In a recent development, not in CA, but we use solar, time of use, and EVs to minimize our energy costs. We’re not feeding power back to the grid from our cars, but the combo of TOU, solar and EVs does allow us to reduce costs significantly. Solar covers all the expensive peak power, I have the cars start charging early enough to use any extra solar, and the rest is off peak at half cost.

Sources indicate that GM is joining CharIN‘s North American AC V2G task force, which is working to align technical standards, equipment certification, and utility approval requirements. In Southern California, the pilot will give GM and its partners a look at how the process works for drivers, from signing up and getting the hardware installed to getting utility approval and sending power back.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the Rivian R2 may be a little tamer than its bigger brothers, the R1S and R1T, but that doesn’t mean that the aftermarket world can’t chime in and lend a helping hand. While the mid-size SUV carried over many of its larger siblings’ characteristics, it lacks one feature that could make the difference between getting back home the same day and spending hours trying to get unstuck: adjustable air suspension.

The R2 comes with fixed suspension, so the driver has to be very careful when choosing their lines, but thankfully, there are now a handful of companies out there that sell suspension lift kits for the R2.

Bullray Manufacturing made a custom lift kit for a Rivian R2 that’s used as a chase truck for the Off Grid racing team. The electric SUV, an R2 Performance, made an appearance at this year’s SEMA show in Las Vegas and was filmed by Out of Spec Bits.

Sources indicate that the 2.0-inch metal lifters were fitted above the dampers, and the electric crossover retains its standard semi-active suspension. In other words, this is a body lift, not a suspension lift, but it shouldn’t matter too much, considering this is a unibody vehicle, after all. The high-voltage battery and electric motors are fitted directly to the underside of the body, so the added ground clearance should help protect vital components when going off the beaten track.

It’s also worth noting that EV Sportline, a tech giant that specializes in aftermarket parts for electric vehicles, offers a 1.6-inch body lift kit for the Rivian R2.

Getting back to the green R2 that went to SEMA, it’s obvious that it’s fully kitted out for any overlanding experience. There’s a Baja Designs 40-inch light bar, a set of Maxtrax Extreme recovery boards, plenty of storage options on the roof, and a Rig’D tire carrier at the rear. A set of Yokohama Geolandar Mud-Terrain tires wrapped around 17-inch Method Racing wheels completes the look.

Inside, there’s a communications system, as well as a racing-spec GPS navigation system for the front passenger.

All in all, it looks really badass and shows that there’s a lot of potential in the aftermarket space for the Rivian R2. Clearly, the raised ride height and chunky tires will eat into the car’s official 330-mile range, but that’s to be expected.

Recent findings suggest that for the uninitiated, Inner Mongolia North Hauler Joint Stock Co., Ltd. (NHL) is a Chinese heavy equipment manufacturer specializing in the enormous rigid-frame haul trucks used in open-pit mining operations. Established in 1988, NHL has decades of experience building mining trucks for customers around the world, including some of the industry’s largest diesel-electric hybrids. The brand’s new NTE240E is different, representing a organization’s real push into battery-electric mining equipment, and it’s powering that push with some seriously ambitious technology.

Industry observers note that let’s start with the battery. The NTE240E packs an absolutely MASSIVE battery pack, with the highest-capacity versions offering up to 4,100 kWh (4.1 MWh) of onboard energy storage. Keeping that much battery topped off is no small task, which is why NHL developed an equally ambitious energy replenishment strategy supporting dual-gun MCS charging, allowing its town-sized battery to go from 20% to 90% in under an hour.

That means operators can take advantage of shift changes and scheduled rest breaks to top off the battery without sacrificing an entire work shift to charging – but even more impressive than the fact that all that juice can be crammed into so major a battery in so little time is the fact that, according to NHL, it can be done at just 25°C (about 77°F).

Recent findings suggest that plugging in isn’t the only way the NTE240E drinks its juice. NHL’s fresh dynamic power reception system uses overhead current collectors to supply electricity directly to the truck while it’s climbing loaded mine roads, allowing it to then “ride the brakes” for more energy all the way downhill.

In a recent development, the combined technologies allow NHL’s operators to keep the massive trucks moving without relying entirely on their onboard batteries. The result is a claimed 15% improvement in energy efficiency over the ultra-class industry average.

Recent findings suggest that that efficiency turns into savings, which means the economics of running an NTE240E could be just as compelling as the emissions savings – and those are substantial. NHL indicates each NTE240E can reduce harmful carbon emissions by more than 2,000 tons annually, even as it cuts operating costs by more than 60% compared to a comparably capable diesel.

Industry observers note that what’s more, because the big BEV’s electrical system eliminates the need for engine-related hardware like generators and the maintenance and overhaul costs associated with those components. Taken as a whole, the NHL seems to be a compelling offering … but that’s not for me to say. You guys are the experts – let us know what you think of the new NHL NTE240E, in the comments.

“The Sierra Club thanks the Senators, Tribes, and advocates across the country who raised their voices in the fight to fix this bill. Americans deserve a better deal.”.

If you're like me, you've been spending pretty much whatever free time you've had since midnight on Thursday playing Grand Theft Auto 6, and while it's much different than the GTA games that have come before it, in one regard it is still very similar. As is GTA tradition, there are no real cars in this game. Sure, everything in there is a vague approximation of a real car, but you will not find any actual brands or models for a plethora of reasons, and that's what led me to today's question.

I want to know what the one real vehicle is that you wish you could drive in Grand Theft Auto 6. Obviously, there are analogs that are close to whatever you might choose, but it's never going to be 100% the same, and that's why I'm posing this question to you today. GTA creates a universe where you can do or be just about anything you want, so it's sort of a bummer that you can't quite drive the car of your dreams in it.

Picking any real car to drive in GTA 6 is a tough task — I know I'm asking a lot of you, but I think for me, I think it would have to be a Ferrari Testarossa... in white, of course. Given the fact that 6 takes place in (theoretically) Florida, it only makes sense to drive a white Ferrari.

According to recent reports, yes, I know that technically it's driven by cops in Miami Vice and you're very much playing criminals (with hearts of gold) in GTA 6, but it still just feels right to me. Plus, listening to a massive flat-12 motor scream as you blast through Leonida would just be spectacular. I'm not interested in your disagreements.

#542. The EV Takeover Is Taking Shape, Despite Heroic Efforts To Stop It

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1099 w)
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cleantechnica

The EV Takeover Is Taking Shape, Despite Heroic Efforts To Stop It

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1099 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Whelp, the AI boom has had one positive knock-on effect.
  • Sources indicate that I’m just going to stick my neck out and say that the eponymous Aptera solar-powered autocycle from the US startup Aptera will attract enough AI-enriched drivers to make a go of it.
  • Autocycles were once common here in the US and overseas markets, distinguished from motorcycles by their front-facing seats and steering wheels, rather than straddled seats and handlebars.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Whelp, the AI boom has had one positive knock-on effect. It is creating newly introduced multi-millionaires by the bushel, any one of whom can afford to splurge on a pricey new electric vehicle. That aside, EV stakeholders in the US are springing back to life after a year-long slumber. Even General Motors is in play, stirring up long lost memories of its 1990’s-era EV1 debacle instead of hiding its head in shame. What’s up with that?

Sources indicate that I’m just going to stick my neck out and say that the eponymous Aptera solar-powered autocycle from the US startup Aptera will attract enough AI-enriched drivers to make a go of it. The on-again, off-again, on-again automaker has been on this year, working towards volume production of a plug-in, three-wheeled two-seater EV that can travel up to 40 miles on its own solar-plus-storage system (see more Aptera news here).

Autocycles were once common here in the US and overseas markets, distinguished from motorcycles by their front-facing seats and steering wheels, rather than straddled seats and handlebars. They fell out of favor in the US by the middle of the 20th century, but 21st century hot-rodders have revived the form with a focus on eyebrow-raising, open-air, gas-guzzling showpieces. In particular, interest has spread in states that do not require autocycle drivers to invest in an additional motorcycle license.

According to recent reports, the Aptera is showy in its own right, resembling a rocket ship with unique aerodynamic styling. Perhaps it may even show up in the next James Bond adventure with James Pattinson at the wheel. In the meantime, the firm has just made good on its pledge to reward early investors in the world’s first solar-powered car with the first production models to role off the assembly line. Aptera #1 goes to the founder and CEO of GDP Venture, Martin Hartono, aka “Accelerator #1.”.

Drivers can reserve an Aptera of their own for just $100, and they can expect to pay about $40,000 for the ride. Considering that the solar fuel is free, anyone in the mood for a head-turning ride will get quite a bargain for their $40,000 compared to other competitors in the zero emission two-seater field, such as the recently refreshed Tesla Roadster.

Speaking of refresh, General Motors has been weirdly lavishing attention on the EV1 sedan all this year, even though the automaker has been roundly criticized for the killing the short-lived car in its cradle. The automaker began producing EV1 electric sedans starting in 1996, following the unveiling of its Impact electric concept car in 1990. Unlike the Impact, EV1 was designed for use on the road. However, it was also designed mainly for the California market, and primarily for lease, not for sale. Production halted in 2003 at just about 1,000 vehicles, all to be recalled by GM and sent to the crusher as chronicled in Chris Paine’s 2006 documentary, “Who Killed The Electric Car?”.

Or, maybe not so weird after all. GM’s electrification journey long predates the launch of Tesla Motors in 2003. The legacy automaker is now determined to stake out its claim on automotive history, with 2026 marking the 30th anniversary of the start of EV1 production.

GM has been celebrating the anniversary all this year with multiple long form articles about the Impact and EV1 on its website, eager to remind everybody that its industry-leading vehicle electrification efforts of the 1990’s continue to manifest decades later, in the form of heat pumps for climate control, by-wire technology, and regenerative braking among other elements.

GM’s latest love letter to the EV1 popped up on November 17, when the automaker officially celebrated the completed restoration of the EV1 “V212” alongside its a private owner, Billy Caruso. The rare survivor of GM’s the junkyard crusher was evidently hiding out in an impound lot in Georgia all these years, until Caruso acquired it at auction and enlisted Jared Pink of the popular show The Questionable Garage to fix it up. Considering TQG’s large following on YouTube, GM wisely lent its engineers to the effort, along with several donated parts from its own EV1.

US President Donald Trump and the Republican majority in Congress have made a heroic effort to dial down the vehicle electrification movement, but facts on the ground keep getting in their way. For starters, today’s advanced batteries apply across multiple energy resources, fossil and non-fossil alike. So, it’s no surprise to see the US Department of Energy continuing to throw taxpayer dollars at latest energy storage projects (here’s one example), even though some of that activity will eventually ripple into the vehicle electrification field.

The US Department of Defense is also getting into the act. DoD’s electrification journey has been a tedious one, but in recent years it has begun creeping stealthily towards a vision of ground mobility enabled by electricity, providing the key tactical advantages of silent running and a low heat signature.

According to recent reports, the latest news on that score involves a $1.4 billion loan commitment from DoD’s Office of Strategic Capital (OSC), enabling the silicon-based battery materials startup Sila to vault its signature product into commercial production. DoD’s primary interest in the company consists of applications in the electric drone and autonomous mobility fields, but Sila has long been eyeballing the EV market as well.

Industry observers note that sila secured the loan commitment in August, and it has not let the grass grow under its feet. On November 18 the tech giant announced an off-take agreement with the well-known Tesla EV battery supplier Panasonic Energy Corporation of North America. “The multi-year agreement is part of a long-term commercial relationship with the potential for over $1 billion of offtake over time,” Sila explained in a press statement, further elaborating that Panasonic will deploy its proprietary Titan Silicon silicon-carbon anode material in battery cells.

“The partnership is also expected to support significant manufacturing and construction job creation in the United States. With Sila’s U.S.-based anode production underpinned by proprietary American technology and know-how, Panasonic and its OEM customers gain a clearer path toward a more secure, resilient, and sustainable domestic supply chain,” Sila emphasized.

Industry observers note that that’s…interesting! Aside from Tesla as one of Sila’s OEM customers, keep an eye on another Panasonic offtaker, the up-and-comer US startup Harbinger Motors, which also has a foot in the DoD door.

Photo: The vehicle electrification movement is far from over in the US, with the startup Aptera among the stakeholders betting on an EV sales rebound in the coming years (cropped, courtesy of Aptera).

The Remnants Of The Electric Saab That Never Was Are Going Up For Auction

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (592 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Insideevs

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that I don’t really know why, but I’ve always been fascinated by Saab, the ill-fated Swedish car manufacturer.
  • In any case, the Saab car brand has been dead for precisely a decade, but now an auction is selling off a unique piece of automotive history that has deep ties to the now-defunct marque.
  • The entire Emily GT project, which surfaced in 2023 after being developed in secrecy for half a decade, is being auctioned off in Sweden by Klaravik.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that I don’t really know why, but I’ve always been fascinated by Saab, the ill-fated Swedish car manufacturer. Maybe it’s because it was always a little left-field, even when it was part of General Motors, or maybe I liked the cars’ design.

In any case, the Saab car brand has been dead for precisely a decade, but now an auction is selling off a unique piece of automotive history that has deep ties to the now-defunct marque.

The entire Emily GT project, which surfaced in 2023 after being developed in secrecy for half a decade, is being auctioned off in Sweden by Klaravik. The lot includes a working mule prototype, bodies, parts, accessories, drawings, and four complete Emily GT prototypes, which are billed as the only ones that will ever be available on the open market.

According to recent reports, developed by ex-Saab engineers who worked at NEVS, the firm that picked up the pieces after the storied automaker’s bankruptcy in 2012, the Emily GT was envisioned as a next-generation electric model with four in-wheel motors and a driving range of up to 600 miles, courtesy of a high-voltage battery that could, in theory, top out at 175 kilowatt-hours. According to technical drawings obtained by SaabPlanet, the standard-range car would have had a 105-kWh pack, while the mid-spec model was designed for a 140-kWh pack.

Wireless charging at up to 11 kW was also in the cards, and no fewer than four body styles, including a shooting brake, a sporty sedan, a two-door coupe, and a cabriolet.

Sources indicate that the four electric motors, developing a combined 490 horsepower, enabled a quite sophisticated torque vectoring system, leading to great road manners. However, none of it materialized. NEVS never had the cash to move forward with the project, and now all of the pieces are being sold off.

It has been revealed that “For us, this is a historic event, and I believe many Saab fans feel the same way,” mentioned Nina Selander, CEO of NEVS. “Despite only ever being built as a handful of prototypes, the Emily GT has achieved iconic status. That notes a lot about the fascination with the car. By making the sale available in this way, we hope to attract car enthusiasts all over the world whose hearts beat for Saab.”.

For the right buyer, it’s the perfect starter kit for a newly introduced car firm, but it won’t come cheap. According to the Swedish local newspaper Ttela, the starting bid will be roughly $1.5 million (15 million SEK), and the auction house is not splitting the lot’s components into individual pieces. Everything is bundled into a single lot, so whoever has the highest bid goes home with everything.

Separately, Klaravik is auctioning off the world’s only NEVS Sango, a prototype of a self-driving vehicle designed for public transport that never materialized.

Both online auctions will go live on November 25 and will run through December 9.

#539. Mercedes-Benz's Point-To-Point Assisted Driving System Is Tomorrow's Co-Pilot In Training

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (922 w)
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Jalopnik

Mercedes-Benz's Point-To-Point Assisted Driving System Is Tomorrow's Co-Pilot In Training

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (922 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • One of my lingering concerns with any self-proclaimed autonomous driving system is losing control.
  • MB.Drive Assist Pro relies on an extensive suite of eight cameras, 12 ultrasonic sensors, a mid-range radar, four corner radars, and, of course, a software stack co-developed with Nvidia.
  • Full disclosure: Mercedes-Benz flew me out to San Francisco, California, and put me up in a hotel on the Embarcadero to experience its latest MB.Drive Assist Pro offerings and the bumper-to-bumper traffic over the Bay Bridge.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of my lingering concerns with any self-proclaimed autonomous driving system is losing control. Far too many times, I've fought lane-keeping assist through highway construction zones, but one automaker might have found the sweet spot: Mercedes-Benz is starting to roll out Point-To-Point Assisted Driving for its MB.Drive Assist Pro advanced driver-assistance system. The feature is impressive for a "Level 2++" system and lets drivers nudge their vehicles through precarious situations that would leave similar Tesla systems flustered.

MB.Drive Assist Pro relies on an extensive suite of eight cameras, 12 ultrasonic sensors, a mid-range radar, four corner radars, and, of course, a software stack co-developed with Nvidia. The semi-autonomous system doesn't rely on a cloud connection, leveraging an onboard high-performance computer capable of up to 254 TOPS, or 254 trillion operations per second. Mercedes has even grander ambitions in its sights with continued development of its SAE Level 3 MB.Drive Pilot system, eventual release of an SAE Level 4 system, and a robo-limousine ecosystem.

Full disclosure: Mercedes-Benz flew me out to San Francisco, California, and put me up in a hotel on the Embarcadero to experience its latest MB.Drive Assist Pro offerings and the bumper-to-bumper traffic over the Bay Bridge.

Industry observers note that point-To-Point Assisted Driving does what it notes on the box. A driver can select a point in the navigation system and their MB.OS-equipped vehicle will drive them there. Over an hour's drive through the hilly, chaotic streets of San Francisco, I sat in the driver's seat of a Mercedes-Benz GLC EV as it safely navigated unprotected left turns and waited at stop signs for pedestrians to cross intersections. Sadly, the software hasn't quite got the California roll down yet.

The system operated exceptionally well, but it's not flawless. I had to intervene twice during the drive. First, the GLC misjudged the distance between a stopped bus and an upcoming intersection on a two-way street, and attempted to pass in the oncoming lane before sighting there wasn't enough room to slot in front of the bus. Second, the GLC detected a phantom stop sign and gradually stopped in the middle of the street.

In a recent development, this is where Point-To-Point Assisted Driving's best fallback came into play: you behind the wheel. In both situations, I was able to easily drive my way out without deactivating the Point-To-Point drive. The system encourages nudging. If your car comes to a stop at a non-existent intersection, you can simply tap the throttle and the car will continue on. You can also nudge the steering wheel to keep your distance from parked cars or puddles near pedestrians. Mercedes refers to the feature as cooperative steering.

While the Pro level receives point-to-point assisted driving, Mercedes also introduced hands-free highway driving for the mid-tier MB.Drive Assist option. MB.OS-equipped vehicles can operate semi-autonomously at speeds up to 85 miles per hour. The system also uses proactive lane changes so cars can maneuver into ideal lanes to approach exits and pass slower traffic; drivers can trigger lane changes themselves by using their turn signals. It honestly makes cruising down the interstate a breeze. I only had a slight scare when I got off I-880 and the car attacked the exit lane near the speed limit as traffic crawled in the adjacent lane. The software can be far more confident than a human, who would be wary of an impatient driver suddenly pulling into the exit lane.

According to recent reports, it should be noted that both MB.Drive Assist and MB.Drive Assist Pro aren't truly hands-free, requiring the driver to touch the steering wheel occasionally. A typically green symbol on the dash will turn red, and if the visual warning is ignored, an audible beep sounds. Then, if there's still no contact with the wheel, the car will pull over and the Point-To-Point Assist will be soft-locked. The feature will only unlock and become available if the car is restarted.

It might sound extreme for Mercedes to lock a driver out of their vehicle's semi-autonomous feature if they ignore system warnings, but it's out of an abundance of caution. The German automaker wants to ensure that it has the safest software on the road, going above and beyond Euro NCAP and U.S. NCAP standards. On an empty dockyard in Alameda, Mercedes engineers set up a dummy-filled test range to showcase its suite of ADAS safety features.

It has been revealed that mercedes vehicles could react to pedestrians in traffic at a moment's notice. Automated emergency braking was still effective at highway speeds and avoided motorcycle riders darting from blind spots across the vehicle's nose. The software suite can even judge with steering away would be safer than braking. MB.Drive Assist comes with impressive creature comforts, like a 360-degree parking camera, rim protection warning, and parking and reverse assists.

These safety features are standard as MB.Drive on all MB.OS-equipped vehicles. MB.Drive Assist is optional on 2027 CLA, GLB, GLC, GLE and C-Class, as well as standard on the S-Class, GLS, and the AMG GT 4-door Coupe. MB.Drive Assist Pro is currently optional on CLA, GLC, GLE, GLS and S-Class, and the firm claims that availability will be wider for the 2028 model year.

Recent findings suggest that mercedes has yet to reveal how much the optional subscriptions will cost vehicle owners. The automaker is rolling out the newly introduced systems in December with an early access program available to selected participants in California, Stuttgart and Munich, before nationwide rollouts next year through an over-the-air revision.

#538. Breaking: GM Prepares For Life Without CEO Mary Barra
