Breaking: GM Prepares For Life Without CEO Mary Barra

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2121 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It's Thursday, November 19, 2026, and this is The Morning Shift, your daily roundup of the top automotive headlines from around the world, in one place.
  • In this morning's edition, General Motors is trying to figure out what its world without Mary Barra in it would look like, over 1,500 Rockstar employees are voting on whether to unionize as Grand Theft Auto 6 goes live, German automakers are staring down the barrel of a work stoppage as a labor fight takes hold and Ford has started shipping the battery cells it's building in partnership with China's CATL.
  • It has been revealed that mary Barra has been the CEO of General Motors for nearly 13 years at this point.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that good morning! It's Thursday, November 19, 2026, and this is The Morning Shift, your daily roundup of the top automotive headlines from around the world, in one place. This is where you'll find the most key stories that are shaping the way Americans drive and get around.

In this morning's edition, General Motors is trying to figure out what its world without Mary Barra in it would look like, over 1,500 Rockstar employees are voting on whether to unionize as Grand Theft Auto 6 goes live, German automakers are staring down the barrel of a work stoppage as a labor fight takes hold and Ford has started shipping the battery cells it's building in partnership with China's CATL.

It has been revealed that mary Barra has been the CEO of General Motors for nearly 13 years at this point. For some, it's hard to think of modern GM without her, but with her 65th birthday just a month away, folks within The General are clearly starting to do so. The automaker is working with an executive search firm to look for possible outside candidates to succeed Barra as it prepares for a future that'll come once the highest-paid Significant Three CEO hangs it up. Don't worry, current GM employee, the manufacturer is also looking at internal candidates.

Barra has apparently been laying the groundwork for months to hand over the keys to the company. She's already GM's second-longest tenured CEO — beaten out only by its first CEO, Alfred P. Sloan, Jr., who was in the position for 23 years. Still, her tenure is about twice that of the average modern CEO of an S&P 500 company, and she's the first woman to run a global automaker. So far, GM hasn't indicated publicly when Barra could step away from her post. From The Wall Street Journal:.

GM has historically groomed chief executives from its own ranks, and internal candidates remain in the mix. Contenders have included the firm's finance chief Paul Jacobson; Sterling Anderson, a high-profile Silicon Valley hire who serves as Chief Product Officer; and Mark Reuss, a 40-year GM veteran and Barra's No. 2, according to separate people familiar with the matter.

Barra took over as GM was still rebuilding after its 2009 bankruptcy and has led the Detroit automaker through trade wars, the global pandemic and tumultuous forays into electric and autonomous vehicles.

GM's stock, up 25% from a year ago, has risen about 136% since she took the reins, and the organization has returned tens of billions to investors through sweeping buybacks.

Sources indicate that barra took over with a mandate to shake up the automaker's notoriously hidebound corporate culture. Her GM has emerged as a smaller but more profitable automaker anchored by its lucrative U.S. truck business.

Industry observers note that GM is selling millions fewer vehicles around the world than it was a decade ago, after retreating from unprofitable foreign markets while slashing low-margin sedans and other slow sellers in the U.S. Yet it is generating record levels of cash and turning bigger profits despite fewer sales.

The firm has spent the past decade trying to pivot away from its roots as a traditional car manufacturer and instead remake itself into a software-driven tech enterprise—a push marked by a string of Silicon Valley hires, an expanding California hub and heavy bets on autonomous driving and digital services.

Of course, not all of Barra's gambles have worked out. GM lost billions on its Cruise robotaxi division before pulling the plug, and its original electric vehicle prepares have been a bit of a disaster that cost the automaker $6 billion in write-downs. WSJ also notes that several of the high-profile tech hires it made saw relatively short tenures.

Industry observers note that barra and GM are clearly playing things close to the chest. Just a few months ago, the CEO was asked if she's considering stepping down, and she told Fortune magazine that she remains energized.

"I still feel like I can contribute and continue to build the foundation," she told the outlet.

We'll see how long she continues, but the $48.2 million in realized compensation she made in 2025 certainly helps.

In a recent development, unless you're at Patrick Star's house, you're aware that Grand Theft Auto 6 introduced at midnight, and it's one of the biggest video game releases ever. In preorder sales alone, GTA 6 generated over $1.6 billion in revenue, and that number is sure to climb as folks buy it in the coming days. Even with all that immense amount of money, workers at Rockstar, the studio behind GTA, don't think they're getting their fair cut. That's why over 1,600 Rockstar employees in the UK are voting on whether to form a union, and if it wins recognition when the ballot closes on November 26, the Rockstar Games Workers Union would be the largest in the UK gaming sector.

According to recent reports, in an op-ed for The Guardian, Rockstar animation programmer and union representative Nestor Uriarte said the studio's reason for a unionization push is because of a decade-long realization that "to tackle the industry's mounting challenges we need to come together." He argues that union recognition would help safeguard the working conditions of developers who built GTA 6 over the past decade. From PC Gamer:.

"Behind these numbers are thousands of people whose talent and hard work make the games possible. With a recognized union, we can ensure everyone, across every department, sees a fair share of the success we contributed to," Uriarte said. "Our games are industry-leading. Our wages, conditions and bonuses should be too.".

Working conditions at Rockstar produced one of the early flashpoints in the advancing push for games industry unionization over recent years, sparked by employees' descriptions of its "death march" crunch culture and allegations of sexual assault. While the studio's taken steps towards a healthier workplace in the years since, employees have reported continuing concerns around gender pay gaps, crunch, and nebulous bonuses conditions.

Coinciding with the union vote, a Glasgow tribunal is weighing testimonies in the ongoing legal battle around Rockstar's alleged union-busting and firing of employees who had been involved in organization. Meanwhile, just days before a launch that's projected to earn landmark revenue, Rockstar parent firm 2K reportedly laid off a third of the employees at XCOM and Civilization developer Firaxis.

"It claims a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off," Uriarte said. "But the truth is that workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised.".

In a recent development, "We've heard from colleagues who are nervous that the union is an outside troublemaking force that will threaten the manufacturer," Uriarte noted. "But we're not outsiders. We are hundreds of studio employees who live for Rockstar, its output, and the players. We want to see it succeed.".

Uriarte mentioned that recognition would also provide developers with a greater ability to negotiate the rapid proliferation of AI in game development, which represents an existential threat to workers in an industry where one third of the labor force has been laid off in the past two years.

Solidarity forever, my friends.

Audi and BMW are among the German automakers that are facing 24-hour strikes this week after workers approved industrial action. It's the latest escalation in an intensifying nationwide dispute over pay, benefits and working hours at a time when automakers are already under pressure caused by weak demand, high costs and stiff global competition. Employees are seeking greater flexibility in labor costs and working hours, and the IG Metall union is pushing for higher pay and commitments to project investment and jobs at domestic factories. From Bloomberg:.

IG Metall will halt production Friday at Audi's main Ingolstadt plant and BMW factories in Munich, Dingolfing and Landshut, it said Thursday. Workers at sites operated by Robert Bosch GmbH, ZF Friedrichshafen AG and other industrial firms in Bavaria are also set to walk out for a full day.

In northern Germany, IG Metall has already secured backing for 24-hour strikes at selected plants across Bremen, Hamburg, Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, Schleswig-Holstein and northwestern Lower Saxony.

Major companies in the region include Mercedes-Benz Group AG, which operates a large vehicle plant in Bremen, as well as aircraft manufacturer Airbus SE and shipbuilder TKMS AG & Co. KGaA, though the union hasn't identified which sites will be targeted.

It has been revealed that the union has offered to allow companies to deviate from collective agreements in exchange for commitments to invest in German plants and secure products and jobs, according to IG Metall. Employers haven't taken up that proposal, the union stated.

Industry observers note that IG Metall is demanding a 5% pay increase and higher apprentice wages in Bavaria, and it claims that employers have proposed no permanent increases for the first 20 months, following by a 1.3% raise. That's, uh, less. They're also looking for greater scope to cut special payments and extend working hours.

According to recent reports, this wouldn't be the first such action. Over 118,000 workers participated in an earlier wave of short strikes in Bavaria through last week. The 24-hour walkouts are the first such escalation by IG Metall during a wage round since 2018.

As I was just saying, solidarity forever.

Ford has started producing its lower-cost battery cells at a newly introduced plant in Michigan that are meant to be used in its upcoming Fathom electric pickup truck. The central Michigan facility is owned by Ford, but it uses technology licensed from Chinese battery maker CATL, which hasn't sat right with some lawmakers and officials.

The prismatic-shaped cells made at the Michigan plant have a lithium-iron-phosphate (LFP) chemistry, and they're going to head to Ford's plant in Louisville, Kentucky, to be fitted to Fathom prototypes. From Reuters:.

Several automakers are transitioning to LFP chemistry because it ​costs less than nickel-based batteries and is considered more durable.

US ​Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy wrote in a September letter to ​Ford CEO Jim Farley that his agency was "deeply alarmed" by Ford's reliance on ‌licensed ⁠technology from CATL at its plant in Marshall, Michigan.

Ford called the letter a "wrongheaded attempt to capture headlines," and touted its development of a US battery plant while other automakers continue to ​import batteries from ​China.

Industry observers note that ford's Alan Clarke, ⁠vice president of advanced development projects, told media this week that working with CATL was the ​fastest way to build affordable electric vehicles in ​the US. "CATL ⁠being the biggest in the world, it means that they're the best supplier to get us that technology and help us learn ⁠how ​to produce LFP cells," he remarked.

Seemingly undeterred by the Trump administration's foolishness, Ford notes it will be able to make 40 cells every minute at the battery facility, and a spokesperson for the organization expects them to still be eligible for a federal battery manufacturing tax credit.

Today's a huge day for all of my friends who work at magazines like Car and Driver, Road & Track and MotorTrend. I'm sure they're all over at the Hearst Tower celebrating as we speak. I kid, obviously, those folks aren't really good at the whole "return to office" thing. Anyway, if you want to learn more about how Patty ended up in this mess, head over to History.com.

Fuel prices continue to tumble, but it's not like anyone is going to notice since we're all inside playing GTA 6 today. Still, for people with obligations, I'm sure they'll be excited to know that slightly lower WTI Crude Oil futures and Brent Crude prices, which were sitting at $84 and $93, respectively, at the time of publication, are helping bring things down.

Here's where national average prices stand right now, according to AAA:.

It has been revealed that what this all means is the average price of a gallon of regular gas dropped another 3 cents overnight to $3.72, according to AAA. Diesel saw a similar 3-cent retreat and is now sitting at $5.93.

Obviously, I love Robyn's original version more than life itself, but there's something about the Kings of Leon cover that brings a certain melancholy to the song. Every Bond movie needs a Bond car, though, and we haven't yet seen what Pattinson will drive in his first outing in the role. Bond should drive a 5th gen Civic Type R. It was built in Britain, so it's got that covered.

However, he's a spy. He needs to maintain a low profile. Hence, Civic.

The Valen and the Valiant are both limited editions and would make good movie cars, but they're both a little too boy-racer for Bond. At the end of the day, a DB12 is the Bond car. It's long and lean, it has lots of room for gadgets, it's got class for days, and it's got a screaming V12 for when things get spirited. You can fight bad guys in it, then roll up to the opera.

We have been eagerly awaiting the arrival of Genesis' first full-on hybrid option for a while, as it's been one of the only luxury brands not to launch such a powertrain. The GV80 Hybrid was finally shown off in Korea in August, and now on Thursday at the Los Angeles Auto Show, Genesis has revealed that midsize crossover in U.S.-spec form and held the world premiere of the the even cooler G80 Hybrid sedan, too.

The GV80 and G80 Hybrids will share the same powertrain, which pairs a turbocharged 2.5-liter inline-4 gasoline engine with a 7-speed automatic transmission, a single electric motor and a battery pack of unknown size. It's Hyundai Motor Group's first hybrid system with a liquid-cooled battery, and the system produces a combined 347 horsepower while returning Genesis-claimed efficiency gains of 24% in the GV80 and 30% in the G80, compared to the regulas gas-only models. Official fuel economy estimates for these two hybrids are not available just yet, but Genesis notes both the GV80 SUV and G80 sedan should return a maximum driving range of over 500 miles on a tank of gas.

It has been revealed that genesis claims its turbo hybrid system was "engineered specifically to highlight the brand's longitudinal, rear-wheel-drive-based architecture," and the liquid-cooled battery allows for a higher maximum discharge output when compared to air-cooled batteries. We've already sampled a version of Hyundai Motor Group's turbo-hybrid powertrain in the segment-topping Hyundai Palisade Hybrid. Jalopnik's own Andy Kalmowitz praised that version of the powertrain for its seamless transitions between electric and hybrid operation, which bodes well for the Genesis system and its upgrades.

Industry observers note that in Genesis form, this hybrid setup produces 347 horsepower and 391 pound-feet of torque, which is 18 more horses and 52 more lb-ft of torque than the Palisade's Hybrid system. It's also 47 horsepower more than the G80 and GV80's base turbocharged 2.5-liter four-cylinder powertrain, and it matches the torque output of the top twin-turbo 3.5-liter V6, which Genesis says helps give it "responsive acceleration from a stop.".

Recent findings suggest that both the GV80 and G80 Hybrids will offer buyers adjustable regenerative braking settings, a nice features that is not always found on traditional hybrids, and it has a Smart function that automatically adjusts regenerative braking based on driving conditions. They also have a Stay mode that allows some auxiliary functions like the climate control and multimedia functions to operate without starting the gas engine.

According to recent reports, both the GV80 Hybrid and G80 Hybrid sedan get a redesigned front grille with a new 3D look, new wheel designs, and new exterior colors. The GV80 has new 19-, 20-, and 22-inch wheel designs developed specifically for the Hybrid, and three new exterior colors: Seychelles Beige, Cardiff Green, and Brunswick Green Matte. It also will come with four new two-tone interior color combinations, real wood trim options, and upholstery quilting patterns.

The G80 Hybrid reflects a bigger change when compared to its gasser siblings: it's actually 5.1 inches longer overall than other G80s. Though Genesis doesn't explicitly say where the G80 Hybrid's extra 5.1 inches goes, it's almost certainly a 5.1-inch wheelbase stretch, since that's the same change that was made to the 2027 Genesis G80 Electrified in other markets. (That car was quietly canceled in the U.S. last year due to slow sales, if you'll remember, so we haven't gotten the LWB G80 until now.) That means it will have a limo-like wheelbase of 123.6 inches, or just 1.6 inches shorter than the flagship Genesis G90 sedan. The G80 Hybrid also gets new 18- and 20-inch wheel designs, and new exterior paint options that are inspired by locations and natural elements from around the world like Wadden Gray, Milos Blue, and Barolo Red.

These latest hybrids will provide Genesis buyers with a third powertrain option on both cars, and they'll each be sold in the usual array of trim levels. Standard features include a 27-inch OLED gauge cluster and infotainment screen, and an array of standard active safety features. Genesis hasn't released official North American pricing or availability for either hybrid yet, but we expect pricing to fall between their base turbocharged four-cylinder powertrains and the more expensive twin-turbocharged V6, so somewhere around $70,000 for both models.

  • As with the redesigned Tucson, Hyundai put its entire back into its eighth-generation compact sedan, giving it a distinct and decidedly upmarket look, a premium-feeling interior, a cutting-edge brain with stellar interior tech, and a hybrid powertrain that'll get over 50 mpg, all while maintaining the idea that "affordability is standard," according to Olabisi Boyle, Hyundai's Senior VP of product planning and mobility strategy.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For the most part, economy cars are treated as fairly disposable pieces of equipment meant mostly for getting folks from Point A to Point B. They're not exactly treated with much care during their lives, and when they're used up, they're scuttled off to the nearest junkyard. More likely than not, that same fate will befall the 2027 Hyundai Elantra and 2028 Elantra Hybrid, and I don't think that's fair. Top to bottom and front to back, this little sedan is just far too nice to deserve a fate like that.

As with the redesigned Tucson, Hyundai put its entire back into its eighth-generation compact sedan, giving it a distinct and decidedly upmarket look, a premium-feeling interior, a cutting-edge brain with stellar interior tech, and a hybrid powertrain that'll get over 50 mpg, all while maintaining the idea that "affordability is standard," according to Olabisi Boyle, Hyundai's Senior VP of product planning and mobility strategy. While I haven't driven it yet, the slightly larger new Elantra seems mighty impressive when it comes to the design, feel and specs.

Full Disclosure: Hyundai paid for my food and transportation so I could check out the new Elantra and Tucson at a warehouse in Jersey City, New Jersey.

Sources indicate that the first thing about the new Elantra that will jump out at you about is undoubtedly how it looks. It's the latest example of Hyundai's "Art of Steel" design language that we've previously seen on the China-only Ioniq V, Boulder concept and recently revealed Tucson. Hyundai also told me that the Elantra's design pulls from the N Vision 74 concept, and even though this is a totally different kind of car, you can certainly see those cues, especially in the wide fenders of the rear three-quarter section. The high-performance N version of the Elantra has already been spied, too, and it's going to look sick as hell.

It has been revealed that the Elantra is slightly bigger than it used to be; 3.4 inches longer and 1.2 inches wider, to be exact, with 1.2 inches added to the wheelbase. Hyundai indicates the majority of that extra space goes to the second row, with gains in legroom (1.1 inches), headroom (0.7 inches) and shoulder room for rear-seat occupants, and now folks who accidentally had a kid will be able to better fit a rear-facing car seat.

It has been revealed that despite the extra size and funky angles, the 2027 Elantra still cuts through the air with ease, achieving a 0.26 coefficient of drag. Apparently, H-shaped daytime running lights and taillights are very aerodynamic. Who knew? The wedgey front end, also reminiscent of the N Vision 74, doesn't hurt either, and neither do the flush-mounted door handles.

In a recent development, it all helps explain why the Elantra is a real fuel economy winner whether you're looking at the entry-level gas motor or the optional hybrid. Fitted with 16-inch wheels, the 147-horsepower 2.0-liter inline-4, with the help of a CVT, will return up to 35 mpg combined, according to Hyundai. The 155-hp hybrid's 1.6-liter four-cylinder is mated to a six-speed dual-clutch transmission and 1.49-kWh battery, and Hyundai says it's going to achieve up to 53 mpg combined, which puts it firmly in "really, really good" territory. There's no word on other performance metrics right now, but I wouldn't expect anything too exciting, if I'm honest. The hybrid also comes with a Stay mode that lets you run accessories off the hybrid battery rather than the ICE motor when stationary for longer periods of time.

According to recent reports, while the exterior is full of hard edges and sudden cuts, the interior is a far softer, more inviting place, one that wouldn't look out of position on a car that costs far more than the Elantra's presently unannounced price would suggest. Hyundai calls the furniture-inspired design ethos "Curve of Upholstery," and it's supposed to be all about comfort, simplicity, and minimizing driver distractions. It not only looks pretty thanks to interesting styling and materials choices, but it also feels nice to the touch with solid build quality.

Industry observers note that hyundai says Elantra is a "software-defined vehicle," which is pretty uncommon for an internal-combustion-powered car. Mostly Hyundai's spokespeople talk about its Pleos Connect operating system and its capabilities, like next-gen navigation (and AI assistance crap), and it explains why the interior's focal point is the 12.9-inch infotainment touchscreen in the center of the dash. The left section of the screen serves as a driver display showing speed and other pieces of vehicle information, while the rest of it is a regular infotainment screen with configurable widgets for media, maps, and everything else you can imagine — including things you can't imagine, since Pleos allows owners to download apps created by others.

In a recent development, beneath the center screen are dual wireless 15-watt Qi 2.0 chargers and 100-watt ultra-fast USB-C charging ports for your many important devices, and you can run audio from stated devices into an optional 12-speaker Bang & Olufsen audio system. Not too shabby.

According to recent reports, then, behind the steering wheel is a slim 9.9-inch display that is meant to keep the driver's field of vision uncluttered and only display critical information like speed, as well as radio, map directions or a few other things via widgets. We first saw both of these screens in the Tucson, and they make the Elantra feel far more tech-forward than a usual compact sedan would. Adding to that tech-forwardness is Hyundai's SmartSense suite of driver-assistance systems, which includes the classics like lane-keeping assist, lane centering, adaptive cruise control, forward collision avoidance and blind-spot monitoring.

Industry observers note that at launch, the gas-only Elantra will come in SE, SEL Sport, and Limited flavors. As you may imagine, features and materials get nicer as you move up the range, but the 12.9-inch screen, adaptive cruise control, push-button start and a few other niceties are all standard from the get-go. Coming a bit later (no word on how much later) will be the 2028 Elantra Hybrid, which will come in SE Blue, SEL Sport, and Limited trims. It's the same deal as the gas car, but there's even more as standard, including dual-zone climate control and Stay mode.

I know that right now the Elantra is shiny and fresh, with its covers just pulled off at the 2026 LA Auto Show, and soon it'll face the sorts of abuse that all budget-friendly cars do. Before that happens, enjoy the Elantra and what it has to offer the world, because it's not very often an automaker swings for the fences on a cheap vehicle like this. Yes, vehicles like the Corolla, Civic and Mazda3 are very solid, but they're never exactly inspiring — certainly not from a design perspective, at least.

It has been revealed that the eighth-generation Elantra elevates the segment, and it might force other automakers to rethink their budget vehicles as well. It certainly looks polarizing from the outside, and it won't be for everyone, but it's also distinctive, and that's something that is very hard to come by on a budget. If you're the type of person who appreciates that, plus a comfortable interior and tech that punches well above its weight class, then it's best you start getting ready now, because the Elantra is set to hit U.S. dealers in early 2027.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that remote control trucks are cool and all, but haven't you ever wanted to remote control something bigger? Realer? Well, Volvo Trucks has your number. The tech giant just introduced a upcoming feature that allows operators to remote-control their own heavy-duty vocational truck — so long as it is on a job site, that is, and going under five miles per hour.

Recent findings suggest that volvo's fresh tech, Remote Steer, is just that — a way to steer and control the tech giant's new VNX heavy-duty truck from a gaming style control from outside the vehicle. It may sound like a party trick, but Volvo actually makes a good case for its use: Rather than relying on communication between a driver and a spotter for precision jobs, like aligning a trailer hitch or pouring concrete, Remote Steer allows one person to do both jobs. A worker can stand behind their truck, at the trailer hitch, and use the remote to back the truck up perfectly without any risk of anyone saying "No, no, my left.".

Sources indicate that it wouldn't be Volvo Trucks if safety wasn't first and foremost in mind. The operator is responsible for switching on the system in the cab and linking the cab to a VIN-specific remote control. The remote control is married to only one VIN number, so there can't be an switch-em-up which could result in everything from hilarious shenanigans to untimely death. There is also a very limited range on the controller, as well as emergency stop buttons on both truck and controller. You'll also need to have all the latest and greatest Volvo Trucks tech to make it work, like Volvo Dynamic Steering, I-Shift transmission, electronic braking system, and a Body Builder Module. If you have that stuff, you can get the module installed aftermarket at any time.

Will this truck replace workers on the job site? Probably not. Ideally, Remote Steer will be used on job sites as a way to help existing workers rather than as a way to replace them. If that's the use case the tech sees, it'll likely be a genuine boon to the folks who have to do precision maneuvers on their trucks all day long. Then again, you might not see it at all, as Volvo Trucks, while sold worldwide to the tune of 120,000 trucks last year, has a smaller footprint here in the U.S than competitors like Mack (which is now a part of Volvo Trucks) or Kenworth trucks.

According to recent reports, either way, we hope we get invited to this press drive. Five miles an hour sounds like peanuts and, on the road, it is, but you don't need much more to dig around in a life-size sandbox with your buddies. Volvo's next move should be expanding to front loaders, excavators and Volvo Trucks-branded microbreweries that allow you to dig around and drink an IPA at the same time. The money would print itself.

What some non-car enthusiasts might not realize is that Walker was also a gearhead offscreen, with several vehicles from his collection fetching high-dollar amounts at auctions, such as his 2000 Nissan Skyline R-34 GT-R that sold for $1.357 million in 2023. O'Conner, whose character arc was cop-turned-criminal-turned-cop and criminal car guy, is behind the wheel of a bright green 1995 Mitsubishi Eclipse in the franchise's first entry.

According to recent reports, sadly, that tuner's life was about as short-lived as its 10-second race with Dominic Toretto, as it was destroyed during a drive-by shooting led by the film's antagonist, Johnny Tran. Gone, but NOS forgotten, the lime green loser continues to garner attention long after its 2001 silver screen demise. Recent sightings include the Fast & Furious Exhibit at the Petersen Museum and, as of last night, the finally released "Grand Theft Auto VI." Although you can't touch the display car, you can drive the game version.

The best part is this easter egg is not a mod that you buy or farm achievements to earn. There is no mission to complete. You just have to find it. Oh, and then break into a house to access the garage before unlocking the vehicle with a, um, slim jim or your elbow. Hey, but then it's yours to drive away with.

In a recent development, the nostalgic Eclipse is located in the middle of Vespucci Island, which is just off of Vice City. As you head toward Vice Beach, the home will be on your left. How you get onto the property is left to you. TikToker @schlayerr is one of many to provide step-by-step directions, and his character climbed over the tall privacy hedge. Others seem lucky enough to find the driveway gate already open.

The only vehicle in the garage is the Eclipse, complete with "F&F" signature colors, distinctive graphics, and a massive clothes rack masquerading as a rear wing spoiler. However, some report not seeing the car during their first visit, needing to return later for it to spawn. At first glance, the Mitsubishi looks the part. The in-game Eclipse isn't the real McCoy, though, but rather a very, very impassioned dead ringer of the film fandom version, like so many other cars spotted in GTA 6.

According to recent reports, for example, O'Conner's car had Toyo Tires decals while the GTA 6 version hawks Terada Tires. The massive wing of the real Mitsu is silver and black, while the animated rendition is green and black. Even the graphics, although the same colors, are splashed on slightly differently. The wheels are six-spoked, brushed-aluminum in GTA 6, while the film car featured seven spokes and was bright silver. Furthermore, the game vehicle feels a lot faster than what you'd get from O'Conner's decidedly non-turbo, naturally-aspirated 2.0-liter.

In a recent development, but it doesn't matter. GTA 6 is a vivid representation of real life without using actual names of places and things, so yup, this is Paul's car ... I mean, Brian's. Whatever. Find it and furiously drive it through the streets of Vice City.

Industry observers note that volkswagen introduced the ID. Buzz Beach, a fun spin on its electric van that’s built for camping and overnight stays. However, it won’t be cheap, starting at over $70,000.

Volkswagen’s original microbus became a cultural icon thanks to its open, customizable interior, making it perfect for large families, road trips, camping, and, of course, music festivals.

The ID. Buzz brings the classic Type 2 microbus into the electric era with a retro-upcoming style, modern tech, and a flexible, spacious cabin.

Building on its reputation as a symbol of freedom and adventure, Volkswagen is adding a upcoming member to the electric people mover lineup.

Industry observers note that the latest ID. Buzz Beach “brings adventure into the electric age,” Volkswagen said after introducing the new variant on Thursday. Designed for camping, longer road trips, and overnight stays, the electric van will be available in 5-, 6-, and 7-seat configurations.

Volkswagen remarked it sleeps two comfortably with a removable bed frame and a custom-fitting folding mattress.

The mattress is a decent size at about 6.5 feet long by 4 feet wide (2.0m x 1.2m), roughly the size of an average small double bed.

In the 5-seat configuration, the bed frame tucks away in the trunk, while in the 6- and 7-seat layouts, it’s stored vertically behind the third row of seats.

For camping and other longer stays, Volkswagen added a new Overnight mode that uses the vehicle’s battery to provide up to 48 hours of continuous, off-grid climate control. The new mode can be accessed on the center touchscreen.

It also includes blackout curtains throughout the cabin and ventilation grilles on the front side windows.

It has been revealed that the ID. Buzz Beach offers vehicle-to-load (V2L) capabilities. A 230V power socket adaptor comes standard, letting you power an e-bike, charge a smartphone, run camping equipment, or power other external electronic devices. A camping connector is available as an added option.

To top it off, Volkswagen added a hidden foldable table and chairs set that can be tucked away without taking up internal space.

Industry observers note that volkswagen will open orders for the upcoming ID. Buzz Beach in the UK later this month, starting at £53,955 (excluding VAT), or about $71,000. Including VAT and OTR costs, it will start at £65,837, or roughly $86,500.

without 300+ miles of range: no.

What about those in the US? VW introduced the 2027 ID. Buzz with a new Tourer model that was essentially the same as the Beach variant in the UK, with a fold-out mattress, Overnight mode, blackout curtains, and a table and chairs set.

Industry observers note that however, VW told its US dealers in September that it would be delaying the ID. Buzz’s return until the 2028 model year.

Sources indicate that the 2025 Volkswagen ID. Buzz started at about $60,000 in the US, which is one of the biggest reasons it failed to catch on with buyers. The original VW microbus was an affordable people mover.

A custom camper variant would likely cost more than $70,000. Would you pay $70,000 or more for Volkswagen’s electric camper van?

EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Jalopnik

Industry News: You Can Get A Free Classic Car And Garage In GTA 6, But Only Until Tomorrow

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, it's finally here.
  • It has been revealed that of course, with a name like Grand Theft Auto, the automotive element of the action-packed title hasn't taken a back seat.
  • Like it or not, you've probably encountered the GTA 6 hype in some manner or another.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, it's finally here. Can you believe it, fans of video game carnage? The internet will have to find some other source of amusement other than the "we got so-and-so before we got GTA VI," because guess what? Thirteen years after the release of the previous iteration, Rockstar Games has finally made the sixth installment of the wildly popular Grand Theft Auto franchise available to the masses. Well, those members of the masses with access to a PlayStation 5, a PS5 Pro, an Xbox Series X, or an Xbox Series S, that is. If that describes you, Rockstar might just have a surprise waiting for your first visit to Vice City in GTA 6.

It has been revealed that of course, with a name like Grand Theft Auto, the automotive element of the action-packed title hasn't taken a back seat. We've been spotting the latest cars in GTA 6 since the extended trailer dropped, and connecting them to their real-life counterparts. For a very specific group of early adopters, logging onto the game will yield more than just the excitement of playing the long-awaited title. Rockstar is giving some players a free classic car and a garage to park it in.

Like it or not, you've probably encountered the GTA 6 hype in some manner or another. That is, unless you've been living under a rock. On a deserted island. An island on another planet. The twice-delayed game is a substantial deal, and it's been available for pre-order since June 2026. Rockstar Games is giving out the Vintage Vice City Pack to those players who pre-ordered GTA 6, and it comes with a handful of goodies. Most notably, the pack includes the '55 Vapid Stanier, a two-tone yellow-on-white classic two-door hardtop.

Recent findings suggest that you might take one look at the Vapid Stanier and think, "huh, that looks awfully familiar." There's a reason for that. For starters, the two-tone Stanier is meant to resemble a 1955 Ford Fairlane Club Sedan and serves as a direct nod to the 1955 Oldsmobile Super 88. Not just any Super 88, but the very specific landmark car parked in front of the Avalon Hotel on Ocean Drive in Miami. And why not? Vice City serves as the Miami-based setting for the game, and the real-life Avalon Hotel boasts that its Super 88 is "one of the most photographed cars in America." Of course, the real Super 88 has a convertible top, whereas the game's Vapid Stanier has a painted hardtop.

Sources indicate that the yellow-on-white classic is a fitting way to hit the streets of Vice City, but it's not the only treat in the pack. In addition to the '55 Vapid Stanier, players will get a special garage. Qualifying players will get a task in their Exploration map tab, which will direct them to the Ocean View Hotel. That's where they'll find the classic car and the garage. You'll likely want a garage to safely store your Stanier, too. If the new game is anything like GTA Online, things will likely get quite explode-y.

In a recent development, so, are you afraid you missed your chance? Fret not. If you place your order for GTA 6 today, you can still get your hands on the Vintage Vice City Pack. For now, the offer expires at the end of today. It also doesn't matter if your physical copy of GTA 6 is in the mail; as long as you place your order before the end of the day, you can get the expansion pack.

Industry observers note that now, it might seem outlandish and unrealistic to expect a free classic car and a complimentary garage anywhere other than the fictional state of Leonida. But Rockstar seems to be trying to dial up the realism factor in its latest blockbuster game. Don't believe it? Unlike the campaign or online free-for-all of the fifth Grand Theft Auto title, players will have to fill up cars with gasoline virtually in GTA 6 to keep driving. That's right. No infinitely full gas tanks anymore. We'll just have to see if the Vapid Stanier is a dainty fuel sipper or a guzzler.

If that wasn't enough, Rockstar also wants players to experience more life-like collisions. How? Well, the developers made sure GTA 6 leaned into advanced physics for more realistic car crashes. So, you know, try not to hit stuff in your classic car.

#524. Breaking: BYD’s folding steering wheel isn’t a concept — it’s in a $49K SUV now

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1128 w)
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek

Breaking: BYD’s folding steering wheel isn’t a concept — it’s in a $49K SUV now

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1128 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • BYD rolled out a production SUV today with a steering wheel that folds flat into the dashboard.
  • It has been revealed that automakers and suppliers have been parading folding wheels on concept cars for about a decade.
  • The whole thing hinges on steer-by-wire.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BYD rolled out a production SUV today with a steering wheel that folds flat into the dashboard. It comes standard on the top trim of the Fang Cheng Bao Tai 9, which sells for 329,900 yuan (about $49,000) in China.

It has been revealed that automakers and suppliers have been parading folding wheels on concept cars for about a decade. This is the first one customers can actually order, according to BYD.

The whole thing hinges on steer-by-wire. There’s no steering column physically connecting the wheel to the front wheels, so the wheel is just an input device, and BYD can put it wherever it wants.

According to recent reports, on the Tai 9, it swings through 180 degrees on a hidden hinge and drops into a compartment in the dash in about 10 seconds. A panel closes over it, and a tray table folds out where the wheel used to be. Only the airbag remains outside of the compartment – keeping it useful with the steering wheel deployed or hidden.

It only folds when the vehicle is parked. Fang Cheng Bao pairs it with a driver’s seat that reclines to 165 degrees, so the pitch is simple: fold the wheel, lie back, and eat, nap, or play games while you charge or wait. The brand claims 80% of the driver’s area becomes usable space and rates the folding mechanism for 80,000 cycles.

According to recent reports, when it’s deployed, it’s a regular D-shaped wheel with a full rim and physical buttons. No yoke. That’s a nice change from Tesla and Mercedes, which paired its new steer-by-wire system on the EQS with a yoke.

At the launch event, Fang Cheng Bao general manager Xiong Tianbo remarked the industry had been talking about folding steering wheels since 2016 without ever getting one into mass production. He added that BYD is using the same type of motor it develops for humanoid robots to move the wheel, a first in one of its cars.

Here’s Fang Cheng Bao’s official video of the feature:.

China’s fresh national standard for steering systems took effect on July 1, 2026. It dropped the long-standing requirement for a mechanical link between the steering wheel and the road wheels, as long as the system meets redundancy and fail-safe rules.

Recent findings suggest that before that, steer-by-wire needed special approval. Nio’s ET9 was the first car in China to get it, back in December 2024. In the US, Tesla’s Cybertruck already uses it, and Mercedes is bringing it to the EQS this year.

Folding wheels themselves have stayed on show stands. BYD’s own Denza brand highlighted one on the Z concept at Shanghai in 2025. Autoliv and Tensor called theirs the “world’s first foldable steering wheel” at CES in January, for a Tensor Robocar they expected to reach volume production in the second half of 2026. Hyundai Mobis has been showing one for years.

According to recent reports, tesla went the other way with the Cybercab: no wheel at all. But the prototypes testing on public roads have a Cybertruck steering wheel bolted onto an exposed column, because a human still has to be able to drive.

The Tai 9 is Fang Cheng Bao’s biggest SUV yet. It’s 5,270 mm (207.5 in) long with a 3,130 mm wheelbase and six seats in a 2+2+2 layout. It’s also the first model on BYD’s new DMS hybrid platform.

A 1.5-liter turbo engine works with front and rear electric motors for a combined 400 kW (536 hp), and 0 to 100 km/h takes 4.8 seconds. The 66.48 kWh second-generation Blade battery supports BYD’s flash charging and delivers 310 km (193 miles) of electric range on the WLTC cycle. Rear-wheel steering, LiDAR, and BYD’s God’s Eye B driver assistance system are standard.

According to recent reports, there are three trims: 279,900 yuan (about $41,700), 299,900 yuan, and 329,900 yuan. Only the top one gets the folding wheel.

According to recent reports, fang Cheng Bao sold 43,872 vehicles in October, up 41% year-over-year, mostly on the strength of the Tai 7. That model is now heading overseas: BYD sells it in the UK as the Ti 7. BYD hasn’t said anything about exporting the Tai 9.

It is not only that these technologies are impressive, but it is the speed at which they are being put into market by some of these Chinese car companies like BYD. They are moving further and further away from the competition but its understandable with the insane competition between car makers in China that they almost have to maintain and edge.

Sources indicate that we’ve seen this at pretty much every auto show since the mid-2010s: a steering wheel slides away so the “driver” can relax while the car drives itself. It never shipped, for many reasons, but with steer-by-wire and autonomous driving now becoming reality, BYD is making the jump.

The Tai 9’s wheel only folds when you’re parked, so right now it’s a lounge feature. Recline the seat, stow the wheel, flip out the tray, and watch a movie while you charge. Is that a gimmick? A little. But Chinese EV buyers spend a lot of time in parked cars, and fridges, screens, and lie-flat seats sell cars there for a reason.

The bigger deal is underneath. The wheel can only fold because the Tai 9 is steer-by-wire, and BYD is putting that in a roughly $49,000 family SUV less than five months after China made it legal. After Cybertruck and now Mercedes with the EQS, we might be seeing the first steps of steer-by-wire actually becoming a more widely adopted technology.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that hyundai’s electric SUVs are getting some love. The IONIQ 5 and three-row IONIQ 9 helped the Korean automaker land its first-ever “Best Electric Vehicle Brand” award from US News & World Report for 2027.

“This win showcases the breadth and strength of Hyundai’s SUV and electric lineups,” Alex Kwanten, managing editor at Autos at US News, said after naming it the Best EV Brand and Best SUV Brand for 2027.

This marks the first time Hyundai has earned the Best EV Brand award and the third consecutive win for Best SUV Brand.

Including hybrid and electric vehicles, Hyundai offers ten unique SUVs, “many of them at or near the top of our rankings in those classes for capability, comfort, performance and value,” Kwanten said.

Hyundai’s fully electric SUVs, the IONIQ 5 and IONIQ 9, “in particular, stand out for their combination of style and technology,” he explained.

Hyundai currently offers the IONIQ 5, including the sporty IONIQ 5 N and off-road-focused IONIQ 5 XRT, plus the three-row IONIQ 9.

Although Hyundai discontinued its electric sedan, the IONIQ 6, after the 2025 model year, the fresh high-performance IONIQ 6 N joins the lineup in 2027.

The IONIQ 5 continued to earn praise, taking its third consecutive Best Compact Electric SUV award. Its larger sibling, the IONIQ 9, took the top spot in the midsize electric SUV category.

Hyundai’s IONIQ 5 is the most popular EV in the US this year through September that isn’t a Tesla, ranking third behind the Model Y and Model 3.

Recent findings suggest that why does it continue winning over buyers? The IONIQ 5 checks all the boxes with long-range capabilities, fast charging, and a surprisingly spacious interior with modern tech.

It’s also among the most affordable EVs in the US. Prices for the 2027 Hyundai IONIQ 5 start at just $35,250.

Industry observers note that however, the base price is for the standard-range IONIQ 5 SE with an EPA-estimated range of up to 245 miles. Upgrading to the extended-range SE RWD model costs an extra $2,500, with prices starting at $37,750, but it offers up to 318 miles of range.

The three-row Hyundai IONIQ 9 electric SUV starts at $58,955 with an EPA-estimated range of up to 335 miles.

In a recent development, hyundai’s IONIQ 5 is about the size of a Tesla Model Y, with two rows of seating and space for five passengers. Hyundai’s larger IONIQ 9 offers three rows of seating with six- or seven-seat options.

The larger IONIQ 9 offers up to 163.54 cubic feet of interior passenger volume, compared with up to 106.5 cubic feet in the IONIQ 5.

According to recent reports, both electric SUVs use an 800-volt electrical architecture for ultra-fast charging. The IONIQ 5 can charge from 10% to 80% in about 20 minutes, while the IONIQ 9 takes around 24 minutes using a 350 kW DC fast charger.

Hyundai assembles the IONIQ 5 and IONIQ 9 at the Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America outside of Savannah, Georgia.

When we toured the facility earlier this year, Hyundai told Electrek that its electric SUVs are winning over new buyers at a higher rate than any of its gas or hybrid vehicles.

The IONIQ 5 had a 69.8% conquest rate last year, while the IONIQ 9 had 64.3%. Hyundai’s Elantra N ranked third (61.9%), followed by the Palisade (61.2%) and Kona Electric (60.9%).

Latest Update: Google Maps Is Trying To Shoehorn AI Into Your Road Trips Now

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (553 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If planning that next day trip is just too burdensome a task, don't worry, like every other aspect of our lives now, there's AI for that.
  • Google's newly introduced Ask Maps feature uses its Gemini AI to lay out an entire itinerary for your next trip in Google Maps, whether it's a day-long adventure, to a journey of several days.
  • To get started, all you have to do is Ask Maps to initiative your trip for so many days and suggest what you'd like to do for the trip.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If planning that next day trip is just too burdensome a task, don't worry, like every other aspect of our lives now, there's AI for that. Google announced its latest and greatest AI-driven planning feature that will do the heavy lifting in planning your next trip.

Google's newly introduced Ask Maps feature uses its Gemini AI to lay out an entire itinerary for your next trip in Google Maps, whether it's a day-long adventure, to a journey of several days. Obviously the announcement was timed to provide enough runway for people to put it to use for the upcoming holiday season in the U.S. AAA expects 81.5 million people to travel for the Thanksgiving and the capitalism-fueled Black Friday holiday weekend.

To get started, all you have to do is Ask Maps to initiative your trip for so many days and suggest what you'd like to do for the trip. Google puts it like this:.

Sources indicate that use Ask Maps to plan a day trip for holiday shopping or something more complex — like a three-day road trip with stops for coastal hikes and oceanfront dining. You'll get a day-by-day schedule with insider tips and numbered map pins for each stop, making it easy to visualize the plan. Once you're happy with the itinerary, share it with friends and family, or export it to Google Docs on desktop.

Recent findings suggest that it's that easy. This could be handy for planning a long trip with an electric vehicle and get help with finding charging stations. Or planning that automotive day trip in Detroit. From my quick search, it could use some edits.

In the U.S. you can modify your itinerary in real-time. If some place ends up closed, or you need to make a detour or additional stop, Ask Maps to add or adjust accordingly. It'll also make appointments for you. Need an upcoming day off to be filled with appointments and errands or just let it order the takeout you wanted instead of using whatever other delivery apps are on your phone. Ask Maps will do it all. The only finger you may have to lift is the one typing in the query to Ask Maps to do the work for you. Although, to be honest, you're more likely to ask it to do the task via voice command.

Perhaps the most curious thought surrounding this, aside from humanity's continued loss of curiosity and self-sufficiency while letting Google do the work, is how long will Google serve these trip recommendations organically? 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that hyundai and Kia have some of the strongest hybrid lineups on the market. Why did it take so long for Genesis to get there?

In a recent development, hyundai and Kia hybrids are printing money. Hybrids now account for 29% of all Hyundai sales, a proportion that has grown rapidly over the last few years. But Genesis has so far been left out of the hybrid sales bonanza. No longer. Genesis revealed the G80 and GV80 hybrids on Wednesday, finally entering the fast-growing market for premium hybrids.

The G80 and GV80 are the Genesis brand’s mid-size sedan and SUV, respectively. The G80 competes against cars like the BMW 5 Series and Mercedes E-Class and was—until recently—offered with a fully electric powertrain. That was canned after slow sales, and the GV80 SUV has always been internal-combustion only.

Industry observers note that both models come standard with a 2.5-liter turbocharged gas engine and offer twin-turbo V-6 engines as performance upgrades. The newly introduced hybrid system will slot between these two powertrains. It adds a parallel hybrid setup to the 2.5-liter turbocharged powertrain, delivering a combined total of 347 horsepower. The top-trim V6 produces 375 hp, for reference.

Genesis says the GV80 Hybrid is 24% more efficient than the four-cylinder gas model. For that G80 Hybrid, that number is 30%. Final fuel economy ratings are still to come, but that’s a sizable improvement given the extra power it comes with. And like their gas-powered siblings, all G80s and GV80s come with all-wheel-drive.

All G80 and GV80 Hybrids come standard with all-wheel drive.

According to recent reports, kind of. The 2.5T turbo-hybrid combo is used in other Hyundai products like the Palisade Hybrid, but it is among the newest, most sophisticated powerplants in the tech giant’s stable. But the G80 and GV80 do get some Genesis-exclusive hardware. The Genesis hybrids are the first Hyundai Motor Group (HMG) hybrids to feature liquid-cooled batteries. The vast majority of traditional hybrids use small batteries that are passively air-cooled, but as we know from larger EV batteries, active cooling systems are great for long-term stability. Genesis claims the cooling system also allows it to take advantage of more of the battery’s energy.

Fundamentally, though, the powertrain should feel similar to existing Hyundai and Kia hybrids. Unlike Honda and Toyota hybrids, HMG hybrids still use traditional transmissions rather than e-CVTs. The G80 and GV80 use a seven-speed automatic, rather than the eight-speed auto that’s employed on the gas models.

The new models offer a “Stay” mode that allows you to run the HVAC and radio for extended periods without firing the gas engine, too, and an EV mode for a limited amount of engine-off cruising.

Sources indicate that if you want something that’s more similar to an EV driving experience, Genesis already makes two smaller electric SUVs, the GV60 and Electrified GV70. A third one, the stunning GV90, is coming soon.

But if you want something like a plug-in hybrid, you’ll have to wait for the organization’s extended-range electric vehicles (EREVs). EREVs—which use gasoline engines purely as generators, with no direct mechanical between the engine and wheels—are coming in 2027, Genesis confirmed at the debut event. The company claims they will offer over 640 miles of combined range. EREV fans will have to wait for further details.

The rear seat of the top-trim Genesis G80 Hybrid.

In a recent development, but if you’re a pure hybrid fan, Genesis finally has a couple of real options. Pricing, trim details, and on-sale dates are still to come. Expect to hear more details next year.

#517. Screen Time and Fitness Reshape Grey Matter in Teen Brains

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (949 w)
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Neurosciencenews

Screen Time and Fitness Reshape Grey Matter in Teen Brains

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (949 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Neurosciencenews

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A neuroimaging study reveals that daily screen time, physical activity, and physical fitness leave distinct structural signatures on the developing adolescent brain.
  • Adolescence is a period of profound structural remodeling in the human brain.
  • At the same time, modern teenagers navigate unprecedented daily exposure to smartphones, gaming, and digital media alongside wide variations in physical exercise.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A neuroimaging study reveals that daily screen time, physical activity, and physical fitness leave distinct structural signatures on the developing adolescent brain. Using MRI scans of teenagers aged 16 to 19, researchers found that heavy smart-device usage is associated with reduced grey matter volume in memory-related medial temporal regions alongside altered maturation patterns in frontal and visual cortices.

Source: University of Eastern Finland.

Adolescence is a period of profound structural remodeling in the human brain. Throughout the late teenage years, neural circuits undergo a natural fine-tuning process known as synaptic pruning—trimming away redundant connections to streamline communication, boost processing efficiency, and sharpen executive control.

At the same time, modern teenagers navigate unprecedented daily exposure to smartphones, gaming, and digital media alongside wide variations in physical exercise.

In a neuroimaging investigation conducted at the University of Eastern Finland and Kuopio University Hospital, researchers examined how these everyday lifestyle factors correspond to physical differences in adolescent brain structure.

Led by Doctoral Researcher Hannamari Skog of the Institute of Biomedicine, the study evaluated 44 healthy adolescents aged 16 to 19 (25 girls and 19 boys) drawn from the Physical Activity and Nutrition in Children (PANIC) study and the FitBrain cohort.

Using high-resolution magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to quantify regional grey matter volume alongside validated lifestyle questionnaires and physical fitness testing (including 50-meter shuttle runs and standing long jumps), the researchers uncovered distinct anatomical patterns tied to digital media habits:.

“Excessive screen time and smart device usage may be harmful to the areas of the brain that are involved in memory and learning,” explained Skog.

Sources indicate that however, Skog noted that larger grey matter volume in visual and executive regions during late adolescence is not necessarily advantageous. Because typical teenage brain maturation involves a healthy reduction in grey matter as neural circuits specialize and become more efficient, persistent volume increases in frontal and occipital areas could signal either intensive visual-motor stimulation from apps and games or a developmental delay in cortical pruning.

Industry observers note that “The larger volume in these areas may be particularly related to applications and games that require attention, motor planning and visual information processing,” Skog said. “During normal brain development in adolescence, there is a reduction in grey matter volume and an increase in brain efficiency. The positive link between screen time and the volume of grey matter in these areas may thus also reflect a delay in brain development.”.

Movement and cardiovascular-muscular fitness were also reflected across multiple cortical and subcortical regions:.

Because the study relied on a cross-sectional snapshot of 44 adolescents, the authors emphasize that causal relationships and long-term cognitive outcomes require longitudinal follow-up across adulthood.

“The results provide new information on how everyday lifestyle factors, such as screen time, physical activity and physical fitness, are linked to brain structure in adolescence,” Skog concluded. “However, in light of the results, the connections between lifestyle factors and brain structures in adolescence are complex, and more research is needed to understand their long-term significance.”.

How does heavy screen time affect the teenage brain’s structure?

MRI scans from the University of Eastern Finland show that adolescents with high leisure screen time have smaller grey matter volumes in the medial temporal lobe (critical for memory and learning), alongside larger grey matter volumes in frontal and visual regions, which may reflect either heavy visual-motor gaming demands or a delay in normal adolescent brain pruning.

Why can larger grey matter volume in teenagers sometimes indicate delayed brain development?

According to recent reports, during healthy adolescence, the brain naturally trims away excess grey matter through synaptic pruning to become faster and more efficient. Having unusually large grey matter volumes in frontal decision-making areas during late adolescence can therefore indicate that this natural maturational streamlining is running behind schedule.

How did physical activity and fitness affect brain volume in this study?

Higher overall physical activity was linked to larger volume in the right visual (occipital) cortex, while better physical fitness scores were associated with larger parietal lobe volume (involved in attention and spatial perception) and smaller volumes in the hippocampus and posterior cingulate gyrus.

Associations of screen time, physical activity and neuromuscular fitness with brain structure in adolescents.

To explore the associations of total screen time, smart device use, physical activity, and neuromuscular fitness with brain gray matter volumes in adolescence.

Brain gray matter volumes were assessed using magnetic resonance imaging in 44 healthy adolescents (25 females and 19 males) aged 16–19 years. Physical activity and sedentary behavior questionnaires were used to assess screen time, including smart device use, and physical activity, including organized sports in sports clubs. Neuromuscular fitness was assessed using a score combining results of a 50-m shuttle-run test and a standing long jump test.

It has been revealed that screen time and smart device use were negatively associated with medial temporal lobe volumes but positively associated with supplementary motor cortex and dorsal lateral prefrontal cortex volumes. Screen time was also positively related to left cuneus volume. Total physical activity was positively associated with right inferior occipital gyrus volume, but the association did not remain statistically significant after correction for multiple testing. Neuromuscular fitness was positively associated with parietal lobe volumes but negatively associated with right hippocampus and left posterior cingulate gyrus volumes, but these associations were no longer statistically significant after correction for multiple testing.

It has been revealed that longer screen time was related to lower medial temporal lobe volumes and larger frontal lobe volumes, whereas higher physical activity and better neuromuscular fitness were associated with larger volumes in the parietal and occipital regions. These findings highlight the complex relationships of screen time and physical activity with brain gray matter volumes in adolescence.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kia’s EV lineup covers just about every size and price point, but it believes one thing is still missing: a truly cheap electric car. That’s about to change in 2027, when Kia aims to unveil a new EV that could start at around $22,000 to $24,000.

It’s been 40 years since Kia introduced its first electric vehicle, the Besta EV, created so runners in the 1986 Asian Games wouldn’t have to breathe toxic fumes from the broadcast vehicle.

Kia has come a long way since the Besta EV hit the road, now offering a complete lineup of electric vehicles, from compact SUVs and hatchbacks to vans and three-row SUVs.

In Europe and the UK, Kia’s electric lineup consists of the EV2, EV3, EV4, EV5, EV6, EV9, and PV5 van, but the Korean automaker isn’t done yet.

“With no intention of resting on its laurels,” Kia said, the brand prepares to complete development of its first software-defined vehicle (SDV) by the end of 2027, an all-new B-segment EV hatchback.

It didn’t offer any other details on the upcoming EV, but Ted Lee, Kia’s executive vice president and head of global operations, told Auto Express that Kia and Hyundai are co-developing a newly introduced dedicated EV architecture for an upcoming pair of entry-level electric cars.

Expected to arrive as the Hyundai IONIQ 1 and Kia EV1, the fresh EVs will compete with other entry-level electric cars like the Renault Twingo, which starts at about €20,000.

Lee said the EV1’s price will be highly competitive not just with other entry-level EVs, but also with small gas-powered cars, with prices expected to start in the €20,000 to €22,000 range, or about $22,000 to $24,000. And that’s without government incentives.

The EV2 starts at just €26,600 ($29,500) in Germany and other European markets as Kia’s current entry-level EV, so the price range would make sense.

While it will be Kia’s cheapest EV, Lee promised it would not cut corners in quality, design, or features.

As its first SDV, the EV1 will feature Kia and Hyundai Motor’s latest-generation tech and software. Kia said the electric SDV will offer Level 2+ autonomous driving on highways. In 2029, Kia plans to expand to Level 2++, enabling it to operate in cities.

The new EV will also use Hyundai’s SDV architecture (CODA), the Pleos Connect infotainment system, and Gleo AI, an in-vehicle Agenic AI.

What will the EV1 look like? According to Auto Express, the entry-level EV will look a bit sportier and less boxy than the EV2 SUV. It could draw inspiration from the Vision Meta Turismo concept.

It also apparently won’t be based on the Picanto, Kia’s smallest gas-powered car. The Kia EV1 is expected to bring a unique style to the family.

According to recent reports, this is good to see and makes sense, especially in Europe. I don't think Kia can go wrong making vehicles at so many different price points. It allows them to reach different segments and almost literally have something for almost everyone.

While all of Kia’s current EVs feature its ccNC infotainment system with dual 12.3″ instrument display and infotainment screens, plus a 5″ climate control panel, the EV1 could bring a simpler setup.

According to recent reports, like its other electric models, the EV1 is expected to receive the GT treatment. However, as an entry-level model, it may not use a dual-motor all-wheel-drive setup like the others.

Will Kia bring the EV1 to the US? Don’t get your hopes up. Kia has previously said the B-segment hatchback is designed for Europe. It could even be built alongside the EV2 at Kia’s plant in Slovakia.

Sources indicate that the good news? The EV3, Kia’s compact electric SUV, is now on sale in the US, starting at just $29,890.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that if you're just reading this, you were likely not one of the 43 enlisted soldiers taking advantage of a four-day leave to play "Grand Theft Auto 6," and instead worked a full day at your job and/or took care of other real-life responsibilities. Being late to the party, though, means there's more insight on the internet for your playthrough, telling you to make sure you fill your gas tank, or remember that Flock-like cameras will track you during your crime sprees. In this case, we found a quicker and easier way to take on one of the first car theft missions in the game.

In a recent development, the mission, called "Unwanted Attention," is to steal a beloved red Phoenix from a police impound lot to acquire some misplaced "cargo," i.e. the "like 20 pounds or something" of weed that Cal tells you is hidden somewhere in the car. According to Polygon, this can be done one of two ways. The first — which is not recommended — is to make your presence very known with weapons and a show. The other, much subtler method is acquisition by stealth.

Now, the version Polygon points you toward is doable, but looks to be pretty involved. Its version has you using special machines to get onto the roof and sneaking into an office where you might have to take down a mechanic. However, a favorite YouTuber of mine found a way that's even more chill, with far fewer steps.

Sources indicate that the fun begins when you pull up to the impound lot in Hamlet. First, you'll want to ensure that Jason doesn't have any weapons on his person. Meanwhile, in gameplay, Cal sends a text: "Help her rise from the flames (fire emoji x3)." Polygon's guide tells you your best bet from here is to not hop the impound lot fence, but if no one is around, you can go ahead and scramble over it, like Jacksepticeye did. From here, casually walk through the little lot to the far back right corner, where you'll see some shipment boxes stacked together in a convenient way that leads up to a storage container on the other side of the fence. Climb up and enjoy a view for a beat.

It's not easy to spot upon first glance, but you'll essentially want to look for the white tow truck under the awning tucked toward the farthest wall from where you are standing. The elusive Phoenix is attached behind it. Carefully climb down from the container and walk casually toward the right of the tow truck. You'll want to be careful to avoid being seen or detected by the cop on the left side of the lot.

It has been revealed that just to be safe, you can use your Waink car scanner on your phone to verify the car attached to the truck is indeed the Phoenix. It'll tell you it's a 1977 Imponte Phoenix (or, in real life, a Pontiac Firebird Trans Am, recognizable thanks to the large gold "Screaming Chicken" on the hood). You can easily unhook the Phoenix from the truck.

In a recent development, now all you have to do is get in the car and hot-wire it — the game will tell you how to do so. Take the car toward the impound lot gate (where you came in) to open it, which will take a painstaking minute, especially thanks to all of the attention you have now drawn trying to drive the car out of the lot. Once it's open, get going! Keep an eye out, however, with your newly acquired flock of enthusiastic followers: the police.

Sources indicate that GTA gamers will know you just have to keep on driving to lose these guys. Once you do that, the game will find ways to let you know to take the car to the Hamlet Pay 'N' Spray shop, where you can fix your likely very dented car as you get acclimated to the game. You'll also want to give it a little makeover  so as to avoid drawing any additional attention. Then it's time to deliver the finished product to Brian's garage where you'll collect a $150 cash reward, likely to fund your own makeover, as you'll also need a way to be less identifiable to outsmart the cops. With that all done, your mission is finally complete.

Tech Report: GTA 6 Ultimate Edition Has A Car Upgrade You Can Unlock Right From The Start

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that like other installments in the long-running and beloved series, "Grand Theft Auto 6" is as much about the autos as it is about the grand theft.
  • In a recent development, if you want one of the coolest rides in all of gaming, though, you don't have to work very hard.
  • It has been revealed that while Ultimate Edition owners are spoiled with perhaps the best-looking car in the game, they still have to work for it just a bit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that like other installments in the long-running and beloved series, "Grand Theft Auto 6" is as much about the autos as it is about the grand theft. Sure, the game has a campaign, and the open-world setting makes it tons of fun to run around and commit crimes. But for some people, the biggest draw has always been Rockstar's sweet, sweet, non-licensed but clearly real-world-inspired cars (and planes, bikes, and boats, of course). Throughout the game, you'll find and unlock car customization options of all types, from decals to lighting and beyond.

In a recent development, if you want one of the coolest rides in all of gaming, though, you don't have to work very hard. You just have to shell out the extra $20 to get GTA 6 Ultimate Edition. Doing so gets you early-game access to the coveted and beautiful Ganado Retro Build. This is an exclusive customization of player character Jason's personal '70 Ganado, a Ford Ranchero-like pickup truck that's become an instant classic. Of all the cars of GTA 6, the Ganado Retro Build is especially noteworthy because of what it replaces. It's a major glow up from the well-loved, drab-colored Ganado Jason starts the game with.

It has been revealed that while Ultimate Edition owners are spoiled with perhaps the best-looking car in the game, they still have to work for it just a bit. No matter which version of the game you buy, you start out with Jason's base Vapid Ganado, which isn't in the best condition. To upgrade to the iconic Retro Build, you'll have to drive the Ganado to a location called Coastal Auto Care, found in Key Lento. Just don't forget to fill up on the way, because cars in "Grand Theft Auto 6" don't have infinite fuel. The player is introduced to Coastal Auto Care early on via a mission, and you can find it on your map by filtering for "Mod Shops.".

You can upgrade your Ganado during the "Just a Scratch" mission, or you can visit Coastal Auto Care any time after completing the mission to apply the upgrade. Once you've driven into the garage's entrance, you get the car customization screen. This screen offers you a choice of different customization options, like cosmetics, bodywork, performance, and interior. Instead of choosing any of those, select the "Pro Builds" tab, which offers you the choice between full kits and wheel kits. For Ultimate Edition players, the Ganado Retro Build kit is found under "Full Kits," and it's free to apply. Unfortunately, this classic design and slick color palette is specific to Jason's Ganado, so you can't bring in other cars and apply the Retro Build kit to them.

Once you're cruising around in the sickest car in the game, you'll want to practice defensive driving. GTA 6 has an advanced physics engine for more realistic car crashes, and nobody wants to see such a beautiful car smashed to bits in a fender-bender.

If you're the type of person who likes to try out every car possible, you'll have your work cut out for you in "GTA 6." There are over 300 different rides you can find throughout the course of the game. Some, like the Declasse Akane (inspired by the Chevy Sonic) are pretty unexciting, albeit still fun to commit major crimes in. Others are breath-takers that can help under-thrilled enthusiasts live their exotic and classic driving dreams.

Sources indicate that take the '95 Grotti Cheetah, inspired by the Ferrari Testarossa. This is another Ultimate Edition-only vehicle, but boy is it sick. If you figure you'll probably never drive a real Testarossa without renting one in Vegas, driving the Cheetah around is a fun second-best. Another eye-grabbing option is the obnoxious green Canis Kamacho, inspired by the Jeep Crew Chief 715 concept. It's a solid in-game off-roader that's available in the base game.

Industry observers note that for players with aspirations that extend beyond the asphalt, the Shitzu Squalo is a special boat available to owners of the Ultimate Edition of the game. It's based on the Christ-Craft Stinger 390x and can be found at the docks of Washington Beach. It has a striking pink and blue gradient color scheme, and despite its name, it's not squalid at all. You'll also get access to biplanes, jets, helicopters, and even airboats as you play the game, allowing you to explore the world in whatever style fits your fancy.

The Next Generation Of U.S.-Made EV Batteries Is Getting Closer To Reality

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (422 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Insideevs

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Silicon anodes could be the next big thing in lithium-ion battery tech.
  • On Wednesday, Sila Nanotechnologies confirmed a new multi-year offtake agreement with Panasonic.
  • We've heard a lot about silicon-carbon batteries over the last few months.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Silicon anodes could be the next big thing in lithium-ion battery tech. A latest deal paves the way for those more advanced batteries to be made in the U.S.

On Wednesday, Sila Nanotechnologies confirmed a new multi-year offtake agreement with Panasonic. Sila's role is to supply Panasonic with its silicon-carbon anode material, which the battery giant will use in its U.S. plants to build next-generation battery cells.

We've heard a lot about silicon-carbon batteries over the last few months. Mercedes-Benz bought into the idea, Porsche invested in it too. General Motors is going all-in on the tech, the automaker's battery chief, Kurt Kelty, told us earlier this year. So why the big fuss?

Most lithium-ion batteries use graphite on the anode side. Sila's approach uses silicon, which can hold dramatically more lithium. In theory, that means a more energy-dense battery with no additional weight and faster charging speeds. A win all around.

Sources indicate that but, there is a trade-off in the material. Silicon has a habit of "swelling" as it charges and ages due to the sheer amount of extra lithium it can absorb compared to graphite. Sila says its Titan Silicon anode solves this problem by reducing overall expansion to something more akin to traditional graphite-based anodes. Its anodes already help power some consumer electronics, like Whoop bands.

Industry observers note that the two companies have been working together to commercialize the tech since 2023 when Panasonic first announced plans to procure anode material from Sila. Now, Panasonic plans to procure it at scale.

Sila's facility in Washington was completed in later 2025 with the ability to produce around 2 Gigawatt-hours of battery material. That's enough to manufacture around 26,000 BEV batteries annually, based on a typical EV battery size of 75 kWh. In July, it secured funding to ramp production to up to 250 GWh. If all goes well, Sila states that Panasonic has the option to offtake more than $1 billion in product over time.
