Ford’s first LFP batteries are en route, and the $30,000 Fathom EV pickup will get them first

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (690 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, ford has entered the battery business.
  • According to recent reports, how do you get more out of a battery without adding weight or more cells?
  • Industry observers note that unlike traditional lithium-ion, LFP batteries use no nickel or cobalt, which helps reduce costs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, ford has entered the battery business. The first LFP battery cells are now rolling off the assembly line at Ford’s BlueOval Battery Park plant in Michigan and are headed to power Fathom prototypes in Kentucky.

According to recent reports, how do you get more out of a battery without adding weight or more cells? According to Alan Clarke, Ford’s vice president of advanced development projects, who is also leading its Universal Electric Vehicle (UEV) platform, the answer lies in lithium iron phosphate (LFP) technology.

Industry observers note that unlike traditional lithium-ion, LFP batteries use no nickel or cobalt, which helps reduce costs. They also typically hold up better after years of use and charging.

In a recent development, to make it a reality, Ford turned to CATL, the leading global EV battery manufacturer. Ford uses CATL’s licensed technology and manufacturing expertise at its BlueOval Battery Park Michigan plant.

Ford said it will be the first in the US to deliver LFP batteries for mainstream automotive use, with the battery cells now rolling off the line in Michigan.

The first LFP battery cells are headed to Ford’s Louisville Assembly Plant and will be used to power Fathom prototypes, its first vehicle based on the UEV platform.

In a recent development, ford designed and engineered the Fathom from the ground up for efficiency. As such, it chose prismatic battery cells because they fit directly into the chassis, reducing structural costs.

With cells now being delivered from a plant that it owns and operates, Ford said it will use the knowledge gained in Michigan to support more affordable EVs and Ford Energy, its new battery energy storage business in Kentucky.

At Ford’s newly introduced battery plant in Michigan, assembly lines can deliver 40 cells every minute, making it one of the fastest LFP prismatic battery assembly lines outside China.

Although the accelerated output drives down costs, Ford mentioned employees use AI-powered image recognition and inspection tools to spot defects in real time and maintain quality.

“Our goal is to make defective cells so rare that we track their frequency per billion cells rather than per million,” Ford noted.

With production testing now underway, Ford looks to have the battery pack plant in Michigan up and running in 2027, ahead of schedule.

Ford will open preorders for the Fathom in early 2027, starting at $28,350 for the standard-range model.

CEO Jim Farley mentioned on the company’s third-quarter earnings call last month that the Fathom, Ford’s first vehicle based on the UEV platform, remains on track to launch in Q4 2027.

Recent findings suggest that farley said the Fathom is a “breakthrough product” that’s highly capable and still affordable. The starting MSRP is under $30,000, and the low cost of ownership is perfect for today’s market, he added.

It has been revealed that ford and Slate both producing vehicles with US-produced LFP batteries is a great milestone. Hopefully we can keep pushing our domestic battery supply chain forward.

Ford said the Fathom will offer more interior space than a Toyota RAV4, and it will cost less to own over five years than a three-year-old used Tesla Model Y.

The pickup will be the first vehicle to integrate Apple Maps directly into the navigation system. All versions will be BlueCruise-capable for hands-free driving, with standard Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, plus bidirectional charging capabilities.

Although we have yet to see it, Ford remarked the Fathom features a “large touchscreen display” with easy-to-use navigation.

Ford has not revealed battery specs or range, but we do know the pickup will have an NACS port after several prototypes were spotted at a Tesla Supercharger over the summer.

#460. West Coast Customs turns a Tesla Model 3 into a 1955 Chevy Bel Air

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1100 w)
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek

West Coast Customs turns a Tesla Model 3 into a 1955 Chevy Bel Air

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1100 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • West Coast Customs has finished its first electric Chevy Bel Air, and there’s not much Chevy left under the paint.
  • The result, called Project B-Zero, looks like a ’55 Chevy from the curb and like a Model 3 as soon as you open the door.
  • In the shop’s new video, “The First Ever Electric Bel Air,” founder and CEO Ryan Friedlinghaus explains that a longtime client, Troy Swope, wants to convert an entire car collection to electric and picked the Bel Air to go first.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Coast Customs has finished its first electric Chevy Bel Air, and there’s not much Chevy left under the paint. The Burbank shop cut the body off a Tesla Model 3, kept the entire rolling platform, and set a 1955 Bel Air shell on top of it.

The result, called Project B-Zero, looks like a ’55 Chevy from the curb and like a Model 3 as soon as you open the door. And it charges at Tesla Superchargers.

In the shop’s new video, “The First Ever Electric Bel Air,” founder and CEO Ryan Friedlinghaus explains that a longtime client, Troy Swope, wants to convert an entire car collection to electric and picked the Bel Air to go first. WCC had previously built the same client a Chevelle with a big gas engine.

Friedlinghaus, who drives a Tesla himself, decided against pulling the Model 3’s motors and battery out and fitting them into the old Chevy. Instead, the Tesla stays whole and the Chevy becomes the body kit.

That’s a formula WCC has used for years with gas cars. The shop calls it “old school meets fresh school”: an old GTO body on a new GTO, an old Camaro on a new Camaro, an old Mustang on a new Mustang. B-Zero is the first time it did it with a Tesla underneath.

“It sounds easy, but that process was tedious,” Friedlinghaus said.

In a recent development, before any Chevy sheet metal went on, the crew took the bare Model 3 skateboard for a spin on the streets around the shop, with no doors, no lights and no seatbelts. Friedlinghaus joked about how many safety violations they were racking up. But it drove fine.

Industry observers note that the real headache was the wheelbase. A 1955 Chevy rides on a 115-inch wheelbase, while the Model 3 sits at 113.2 inches. On its gas builds, WCC can cut, shorten or lengthen the newer car’s frame to match the old body. You can’t do that with a Tesla, since the floor is the battery pack.

So the shop changed the body instead, stretching the Bel Air’s rear wheel wells so the wheels sit where they look like they belong.

It has been revealed that the client wanted the exterior to read as a mostly stock Bel Air. The original car was red, so WCC kept it red, with a satin finish and gloss black accents.

Inside, it’s a Model 3. The shop kept the Tesla’s interior, including the steering wheel and center touchscreen, and modified it to fit the Chevy body. The seats got black suede with white stitching in an octagon pattern that Friedlinghaus said was borrowed from the Lamborghini Urus, plus red accents and a “B-Zero” script on the dash.

It has been revealed that friedlinghaus noted the goal was for people to see “a really nice Bel Air” from the outside, then open the door and find a Tesla. He also expects some double takes when it pulls into a Supercharger station.

He admits the reaction has been split. Plenty of people are mad that the shop electrified a Bel Air, and plenty of others think it came out great. The client is clearly in the second camp, describing the car as easy to drive and saying every trip in it feels like an event.

Here’s the full build video from West Coast Customs:.

This is sick. I know Tesla doesn’t care about personal car ownership anymore, but they should really sell their platform so shops can do these conversions without using salvage vehicles.

Industry observers note that well I was really interested in this build until I read how they kept it entirely Tesla inside. Not at all what I was thinking or what I'd call a true old car conversion to EV. Instead, they simply transformed the outside of a Tesla into an old looking car. To me, even the outside looks too far removed from the original Bel Air and more like a street rod. If that's what the owner wants and paid for, great.

Recent findings suggest that but for me, I would never do a conversion like that. I really want to convert an older 70's or 80's or early 90's Cadillac into an EV. But for me, I will insist that the outside and inside look 100% like the original car with just an EV powertrain.

Don’t get me wrong, if you can recycle a salvage, that’s good, but it can’t always be done.

According to recent reports, compare it to the 1966 Mustang that a Sacramento Tesla parts shop converted earlier this year. That project took about $40,000 and two years, with the team grafting sections of a Model 3 floor into the Mustang. It’s an amazing build, but it’s a lot of custom engineering. WCC’s approach skips most of that. You keep Tesla’s crash structure, battery thermal management, software, over-the-air updates and Supercharger access, because you never took the car apart in the first place. It’s closer to what S-Klub did with its Model 3-based Mercedes 300SL than a traditional drivetrain swap.

In a recent development, the purists will hate it. That’s fine. This Bel Air will get driven more in a year than most restored ones get driven in a decade.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that rivian’s upcoming electric bike spinoff, ALSO, has hit another speed bump. The tech giant has declared that it is temporarily halting deliveries of its TM-B electric bicycles after discovering software-related problems affecting some bikes, including challenges with charging behavior.

And unfortunately, this isn’t entirely surprising. We’ve already reported on some strange battery behavior with the latest e-bikes, as well as customers having to send their bikes back for repairs.

In a message sent to customers, ALSO explained that it was pausing shipments to address several software problems before more bikes reach riders.

“We’ve identified a few software-based challenges, such as charging behavior, that are impacting some bikes,” the company explained.

ALSO states its engineers are working on a firmware upgrade to resolve the problems, with shipments expected to resume in approximately two weeks.

The pause affects the remaining Launch Edition deliveries as well as the beginning of Performance Edition shipments, both of which will now arrive later than previously promised.

The announcement follows earlier reports of unusual charging and discharging behavior on the TM-B, which we previously highlighted as some of the growing pains facing Rivian’s ambitious latest e-bike venture.

We’ve also reported on customers needing to return their bikes for repairs, raising questions about how smoothly the firm’s initial rollout was progressing.

The issues align with many of our initial concerns we discussed a year ago when the bike was first unveiled, namely that the high-tech design means the bike incorporates many fresh and proprietary systems that could each lead to complicated and costly failures.

Now ALSO has officially acknowledged software problems affecting some bikes, including charging behavior, though it hasn’t detailed the full extent of the challenges or confirmed whether they are directly related to those earlier reports.

The bike represents a fairly radical departure from traditional electric bicycles, with proprietary technology throughout its drivetrain and control systems. That makes software an especially vital part of the ownership experience.

It has been revealed that to ALSO’s credit, pausing deliveries to fix known problems is probably the right move. Nobody wants to receive a premium-priced electric bicycle only to discover that it needs an immediate trip back to the manufacturer.

But for customers who have already waited longer than expected, another delay is undoubtedly frustrating.

ALSO claims it will provide another upgrade on November 24, hopefully with better news about when deliveries can resume.

#457. Tesla toughens FSD driver monitoring in Europe while loosening it in the US

EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek

Tesla toughens FSD driver monitoring in Europe while loosening it in the US

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1139 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tesla is rolling out stricter driver monitoring for its “Full Self-Driving” system in Europe, with earlier warnings, a full strike for drivers who look away during a manoeuvre, and a hands-on-wheel requirement above 130 km/h (81 mph).
  • It has been revealed that in the US, Tesla has spent the last year going the other way.
  • Sources indicate that on November 16, the Dutch vehicle authority RDW declared that it signed off on a newly introduced update to Tesla Assisted Driving, the name Tesla now uses for FSD (Supervised) in Europe.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla is rolling out stricter driver monitoring for its “Full Self-Driving” system in Europe, with earlier warnings, a full strike for drivers who look away during a manoeuvre, and a hands-on-wheel requirement above 130 km/h (81 mph).

It has been revealed that in the US, Tesla has spent the last year going the other way. Its CEO told owners they can text and drive on FSD, and recent US builds were tuned to nag drivers less.

Sources indicate that on November 16, the Dutch vehicle authority RDW declared that it signed off on a newly introduced update to Tesla Assisted Driving, the name Tesla now uses for FSD (Supervised) in Europe. It covers HW4 vehicles and goes out over the air.

According to recent reports, according to the RDW, drivers now get attention warnings earlier. If a driver isn’t paying attention while the system performs a manoeuvre, they get a “full strike.” The regulator claims the patch also adds measures to prevent misuse of the system, but it didn’t spell out what they are.

There’s a speed component too. Above 130 km/h (where legal), the driver has to keep their hands on the wheel. And setting a maximum speed above what the system displays now requires the driver to confirm it by scrolling the wheel up, with the speed limit sign pulsing red when the car goes over.

It has been revealed that the RDW says it tested the revision on its own track and on public roads and found no adverse or unintended effects. Ten other countries have adopted the Dutch approval so far, with Finland now on the list, while EU-wide approval is still waiting on a vote at the TCMV, the committee of member states.

Industry observers note that this comes two weeks after Tesla cut the system’s speed margin from 50% to 10% over the limit in Europe and dropped the “Full Self-Driving” name there. Germany had made both a condition of supporting EU approval.

Now look at how Tesla handles the same software at home.

At Tesla’s shareholder meeting last November, Musk complained that the car was “a little strict about keeping your eyes on the road” and said Tesla would “allow you to text and drive essentially” within a month or two. A month later, an owner asked whether FSD v14.2.1 allowed texting. Musk’s answer: “Depending on context of surrounding traffic, yes.”.

Texting while driving is illegal in 49 states. FSD is still a Level 2 system, and Tesla’s own fine print notes the driver is responsible at all times.

In a recent development, in May, Musk confirmed that FSD v14.3.3 was built to nag drivers less. Tesla did add better eye-gaze tracking and eyewear handling in a June build, to be fair. But the pitch to owners hasn’t changed: fewer nags is sold as a feature.

And US drivers have been allowed to go hands-free on FSD at any speed since Tesla moved to cabin-camera monitoring in 2024. There’s no 130 km/h rule here.

In a recent development, NHTSA noticed. In its engineering analysis of FSD crashes in low-visibility conditions, the agency asked Tesla to justify a list of its marketing claims, and it specifically cited Musk’s texting post. In September, Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi asked NHTSA to look into Tesla’s driver monitoring after dozens of videos appeared to show drivers asleep on Autopilot and FSD.

Sources indicate that the results are on the road. Last month, a driver told the CHP he was asleep on FSD when his Tesla drove through a freeway closure and hit a patrol car, seriously injuring two officers. Owners are also filming themselves defeating Tesla’s driver monitoring and posting it for clout.

Both markets get the same cabin camera and the same HW4 computer.

But in Europe, a type-approval authority tests every patch before it ships and can refuse it. In the US, nobody pre-approves driver-assist software. Tesla self-certifies, and NHTSA only steps in after complaints and crashes pile up, which is how you end up with a CEO publicly telling owners to text while the regulator is still writing letters about it.

This update proves Tesla can build stricter driver monitoring whenever a regulator demands it. The code exists. It’s running on HW4 cars in 11 European countries right now.

That's because Musk is buddies with the current federal government that would regulate his not-full-self-driving system. Whereas Europe doesn't kowtow to his whims. We'll see what happens in 2029 with a new administration.

That makes the US approach hard to defend. Tesla’s argument for relaxing supervision is that FSD is now good enough. But if that were true, it would be showing the RDW data proving looser monitoring is safe, not adding earlier warnings and harsher strikes to get approved. It’s doing the opposite in Europe because it has to, and the opposite of that in the US because it can.

Industry observers note that we’ve been saying it for a while: FSD gets more dangerous as it gets better, because people trust it more and watch the road less. The answer is monitoring that tightens as the system improves. Europe is forcing exactly that. In the US, Tesla is loosening it, encouraging illegal phone use from the top, and leaving drivers with 100% of the liability when it goes wrong.

In a recent development, so here’s the question for Tesla. If European owners are getting earlier warnings and instant strikes, why not American owners on the exact same software? Or is NHTSA going to have to force it?

Some ledes in this business practically write themselves. An axe-wielding Irishman was charged Tuesday with destruction of government property after he allegedly broke into an airport and smashed the absolute stuffing out of a U.S. Air National Guard C-130 Hercules, destroying the plane outright in the process. The peace activist is alleged to have destroyed the plane over his anger over the U.S. support of Israel and the ongoing war with Iran.

Sources indicate that the Department of Justice says Daithi O'Corrain spent hours smashing dials, snipping wire bundles, and cutting crucial hoses on the behemoth transport plane after breaking into Shannon Airport, located in southwest Ireland, back in April. O'Corrain supposedly really did a number on the plane. The unsealed indictment says O'Corrain poured ball bearings into the fuel tank, destroyed every single one of the delicate dials in the cockpit, and cut the plane's hydraulic lines. The damage was so extensive that the $60 million plane can not be repaired and will be scrapped.

"As alleged, Daithi O'Corrain carried out a deliberate, planned attack against a U.S. military aircraft, causing tens of millions of dollars in damage and jeopardizing critical military operations," remarked FBI Assistant Director in Charge James C. Barnacle, Jr. "This was not an act of spontaneous vandalism. The defendant allegedly spent months researching the aircraft, acquiring tools and materials, and preparing to maximize the destruction he could inflict. The FBI and our law enforcement partners will continue to pursue anyone who targets U.S. military assets, regardless of where those attacks occur.".

Industry observers note that O'Corrain is alleged to have snuck into the plane around 4:40 a.m. on April 11, 2026 after he bashed in the locking mechanism on the rear crew door. He then barricaded himself inside the aircraft, covering the windows with crew member hammocks. After disabling the interior doors with epoxy and ball-bearings, the axe-smashing began. O'Corrain put his whole heart into taking out this plane, to the point that he needed an offsite break before he was back at it the next morning, which is when he was caught.

Several hours after O'CORRAIN first entered the airport, the Aircraft's flight crew (the "Crew") returned to the Aircraft to depart for their next destination, observed O'CORRAIN through a cockpit window, and notified Shannon Airport security. Members of the Crew then observed O'CORRAIN escape out of a hatch in the Aircraft's roof and inflict substantial additional damage to the Aircraft's exterior, including by striking the exterior of the Aircraft with an axe, and pouring unknown substances and placing objects, including ball bearings, into the Aircraft's fuel tanks.

Sources indicate that O'Corrain is currently being held without bail in a Limerick prison where he faces three charges: trespassing at Shannon airport, criminal damage to a fence, and criminal damage to a U.S. military plane. If convicted, he faces up to 10 years in prison.

It has been revealed that O'Corrain is a long-time peace activist who opposes the U.S. war with Iran and the U.S.' support of Israel. He decided to take matters into his own hands, according to friends who set up a legal support fund for O'Corrain. According to the feds, O'Corrain spent weeks planning his assault on the U.S. Air National Guard C-130 Hercules, researching just how to hit it where it would hurt the most.

Ireland was the first European country to recognize Palestine as a state, and the last to grant Israel an embassy. In fact, it is one of the most pro-Palestine countries in the world, NPR reported in 2024:.

It has been revealed that A little over a century ago, Ireland and Palestine were both under British control. The latter was called British Mandate Palestine, or Mandatory Palestine. Many of the same British colonial officials served in both places — and left a deep impression on locals.

For example, former British Prime Minister Arthur Balfour was most famous for something he wrote after he left that office: The 1917 Balfour Declaration, which announced Britain's support for the establishment of a "national home for the Jewish people" in Palestine, a region previously ruled by the Ottomans.

In a recent development, but before his famous declaration, Balfour served in the 1880s as a British Cabinet secretary for Ireland. In 1885, he opposed home rule for Ireland, and his disagreement with colleagues over the problem ultimately helped to topple a previous British prime minister's government.

According to the indictment, O'Corrain's attack follows three other — less serious — incidents at Shannon airport in 2025.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Kia wanted to design a fresh vehicle for the 1986 Asian Games, which were held in Seoul, South Korea, one that did not emit any toxic fumes in front of runners.
  • Recent findings suggest that so, it created the Besta EV.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Kia Besta EV hit the roads in 1986 as the brand’s first fully electric vehicle. 40 years later, Kia continues to “lead the pack” with a full lineup of EVs ranging from entry-level cars and SUVs to three-row models, and just about everything in between.

Kia wanted to design a fresh vehicle for the 1986 Asian Games, which were held in Seoul, South Korea, one that did not emit any toxic fumes in front of runners.

Recent findings suggest that so, it created the Besta EV. The Besta van was initially developed 40 years ago by Kia’s Central Research Institute as the successor to the popular Bongo van, which is still sold in Korea and other markets today.

Unlike the Bongo, it was developed using Kia’s in-house tech rather than sourced from another automaker and rebadged as its own.

Kia swapped the 2.0L four-cylinder diesel engine for a 35 kWh battery and electric motor, which provided a range of more than 26 miles (42 km) on a single charge.

While the Besta EV was never actually sold to the public, it laid the groundwork and offered an early glimpse at Kia’s shift to electrification.

Sources indicate that the first mass-produced Korean EV certified for commercial sale was the Kia Pride EV in 1993. In 2011, the Ray EV became Kia’s first series-production electric car.

Kia expanded its electrification ambitions to Europe and the UK in 2014 with the first-generation Soul EV, the beloved boxy, funky crossover that was discontinued after the 2025 model year.

The Korean automaker has come a long way since the Besta EV, with a full lineup of electric vehicles ranging from compact cars to mid-size and three-row SUVs, vans, and just about everything in between.

Kia now offers an electric option for nearly everyone with seven-passenger EVs on sale in the UK and Europe, including the EV2, EV3, EV4, EV5, EV6, EV9, and PV5 Passenger van.

Industry observers note that with its first software-defined vehicle (SDV) and a newly introduced B-segment electric hatchback set to launch by the end of 2027, Kia has no looks to slow down. On top of this, Kia will expand its PBV lineup with the PV7 next year, a larger sibling to the PV5.

Four decades after the Besta EV arrived, Kia said it continues to “lead the pack today” with one of the most diverse all-electric EV lineups of any brand.

Through October, Kia has sold over 135,000 EVs in the UK, with fully electric vehicles now accounting for over 37% of total sales.

Thanks to its newly introduced EV lineup, Kia became “Europe’s fastest-growing top 10 passenger-car brand.” According to the European Automobile Manufacturers’ Association, Kia registered 377,078 vehicles between January and August 2026, up 9% compared to the same period last year.

Sjoerd Knipping, Chief Operating Officer of Kia Europe, mentioned the growth is thanks to having “one of the broadest and most advanced electrified line-ups in Europe.”.

Recent findings suggest that in the US, Kia launched the compact EV3 (check out our review of it) this year, starting at just $29,890. It joins the EV6, EV9, and Niro EV in Kia’s US electric vehicle lineup.

  • Representative John Moolenaar, the Republican chair and Representative Ro Khanna, the top Democrat on the panel (see what I mean about bipartisan), said that the fact that roughly 20% of Mercedes-Benz was owned by various Chinese investors presents significant risks, according to Reuters.
  • According to recent reports, mercedes, for its part, said it will cooperate.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Republicans and Democrats on Capitol Hill don't agree on much, but for one reason or another, they're all pretty much aligned on the idea that we cannot allow Chinese-made vehicles to enter the United States, and that's causing quite the headache for Mercedes-Benz. Top lawmakers on both sides of the aisle on the House Select Committee on China have asked the mostly German automaker to answer detailed questions about its ties to China and some of its technology partnerships as Congress looks to put a stop to China-owned automakers from selling vehicles here — not that they really were in the first place.

Representative John Moolenaar, the Republican chair and Representative Ro Khanna, the top Democrat on the panel (see what I mean about bipartisan), said that the fact that roughly 20% of Mercedes-Benz was owned by various Chinese investors presents significant risks, according to Reuters. In a letter reviewed by the outlet, the two said that the ownership concern is compounded both "by the specific nature of the shareholders" and the "operational influence they appear to exert" over Mercedes-Benz. To be honest, I think if Mercedes was actually being influenced by China, its sales would probably be better there.

According to recent reports, mercedes, for its part, said it will cooperate. In a statement, the automaker added that it operates independently under the direction of its board of management. Here's what it told Reuters:.

Industry observers note that "Our shareholders have no management board seats and no management authority," the automaker said, adding ​the company "has long supported measures designed to protect U.S. national security, and any suggestion that the company opposes those objectives is incorrect.".

Industry observers note that the committee wants answers to its two dozen questions from Mercedes by December 1. It's also asking for the organization to provide supporting documents and to meet with Mercedes-Benz North American CEO Jason Hoff.

This latest tidbit comes as Congress sets the stage to enshrine an even tougher ban on Chinese vehicles already virtually banned. Lawmakers say that Mercedes' answers would help Congress as it considers legislation "to mitigate the profound threat" posed by Chinese vehicles in the U.S. market. Of course, they don't seem bothered by all of the other Chinese tech products we've already got over here. Nope. Not at all.

According to recent reports, to me, a much more profound threat to the U.S. would be a manufacturer like Mercedes-Benz, which employs about 10,000 folks in the U.S. directly and supports a further 107,000 between suppliers and service providers, suddenly not being able to do business here anymore because of ill-conceived legislation. That legislation, which as we previously covered back in July when it was approved by the Senate Commerce Committee, would ban companies with more than 15% ownership by Chinese entities from selling vehicles in the U.S. Unfortunately for Mercedes-Benz, that's the situation it finds itself in, as state-owned Chinese automaker BAIC owns about 10%, as does Geely chair Li Shufu.

Some seem to understand the implications of nuking a manufacturer like Mercedes from the U.S. market, and perhaps that's why Republican Senator Bernie Moreno (one of the bill's architects) said that the final legislation will ensure that Mercedes isn't banned from the U.S., according to Reuters. He added that there were similar discussions about how Volvo, which is majority-owned by Geely, could continue to sell vehicles in the U.S. Unfortunately, its sister company, Polestar, will not get the same grace period for whatever reason.

At the end of the day, this is all rather silly. Regulation imposed by the Biden administration in early 2025 effectively banned all Chinese automakers from selling passenger vehicles in the U.S., arguing that they could send sensitive drive data to China (as if home-grown automakers aren't taking our data already), and there is a 100% tariff on Chinese EVs that enter the U.S.

Congress and the lobbyists that automakers pay handsomely can take it easy; Chinese cars aren't coming stateside anytime soon.

#449. Why Doesn't GTA 6 Have Licensed Vehicles Despite Rockstar's Immense Wealth?

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (364 w)
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Jalopnik

Why Doesn't GTA 6 Have Licensed Vehicles Despite Rockstar's Immense Wealth?

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (364 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto, as you might imagine, has plenty of extremely cool cars.
  • Sources indicate that rockstar cofounder Jamie King has two reasons: Cost and creativity.
  • There's another reason, though, that King didn't mention: Automakers are picky about how their cars are used in games.

Grand Theft Auto, as you might imagine, has plenty of extremely cool cars. Grand Theft Auto VI brings this focus on its titular Autos even further, with a genuine race track and all the associated automotive accoutrements, but one series trend remains stalwart: No matter how close GTA's cars come to their real-life inspirations, Rockstar Games still won't place real logos or brand names on them. Why not?

Sources indicate that rockstar cofounder Jamie King has two reasons: Cost and creativity. For the former, GTA VI isn't even out yet and per GTABase, fans have already catalogued 317 unique vehicles — Rockstar has plenty of money, sure, but individually licensing each of those makes and models would still take serious cash that could be better used on other aspects of development. For the latter, not slavishly matching existing vehicles allows Rockstar freedom in designing and engineering the cars to better fit a game world. Cars don't need to match their real-world suspension design, drivetrains, or numbers of doors, and can instead tweak those to be better suited for what players need in-game.

There's another reason, though, that King didn't mention: Automakers are picky about how their cars are used in games. Grand Theft Auto is as much about the Grand Theft as the Autos, and carmakers often limit how much their cars can be damaged in-game — "GTA" players would be disappointed if they shot up a car and found it immune to bullet holes, explosions, and fire. By avoiding real-world branded vehicles, and the associated rules automakers place on their intellectual property, Rockstar can build more verisimilitude within its games.

In a recent development, rockstar owns up to cost and creative control as reasons it doesn't license cars for Grand Theft Auto, but freedom to do what it wants with the vehicles in its games is likely just as big a reason. So when you spawn into Leonida tomorrow, and start to wonder why Jason and Lucia's obvious Ford Ranchero is branded as a Vapid Ganado, ask yourself how much worse you'd be willing for GTA VI to be in order to have a Ford badge on that grille.

IONNA enables Plug & Charge for Tesla, opens 22 bay site in Westminster, CA

💡 Key Takeaways
  • IONNA, the DC charging operator backed by several major OEMs, has opened its largest DC charging site yet, with 22 bays of 400kW charging in Westminster, California.
  • Alongside the opening, IONNA is also enabling Plug & Charge operation for Tesla EVs, with Stellantis EVs “coming soon.”.
  • IONNA is a rapidly expanding DC charging network which is garnering good reviews from EV drivers, with clean, fast and easy to use charging stations (which it calls “Rechargeries”).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

IONNA, the DC charging operator backed by several major OEMs, has opened its largest DC charging site yet, with 22 bays of 400kW charging in Westminster, California.

Alongside the opening, IONNA is also enabling Plug & Charge operation for Tesla EVs, with Stellantis EVs “coming soon.”.

IONNA is a rapidly expanding DC charging network which is garnering good reviews from EV drivers, with clean, fast and easy to use charging stations (which it calls “Rechargeries”).

But until now, we haven’t had all that many chargers in the LA area. There are a couple in South OC and the Inland Empire, but nothing closer to the population center of the metro area (though more are opening soon).

That changes now with IONNA’s upcoming flagship charging station in Westminster. It features 12 CCS connectors and 10 NACS ports, so you can charge just about any EV (no Chademo, nor can my AC-only Tesla Roadster charge here… ho hum).

In addition to 22 chargers with peak 400kW capacity, the site features indoor and outdoor lounge space, restrooms, and other amenities like an In N Out and a taco shop across the street. (Not quite as full-featured as my favorite charging station, Rove, but IONNA has a much larger national footprint, and does have faster chargers).

There’s also a small, convenience-store-like area that uses Amazon’s “just walk out” technology. You swipe a card to unlock the room, pick up any items you want, and just walk out. The many cameras on the ceiling track you (and whoever came in with you) and what you’re picking up, then charge your card for the items you took with you.

The store has snacks and drinks, though no ice cream, which is the main thing I’m looking for on a roadtrip stop… IONNA may convert one of the fridges to a freezer in the future, depending on how things go.

And, importantly, the site has trash cans and window wipers – just what you need on a roadtrip stop.

Speaking of roadtrips, the charger opening caps off a cross-country roadtrip by IONNA personnel, who set out in several cars from various parts of the country, all convening on the upcoming Rechargery in Westminster.

Over 20 EVs joined the roadtrip and drove over 40,000 combined miles on their trip to Westminster. The teams charged at approximately 30% of the organization’s charging sites, showing just how easy it is to do roadtrips in an EV.

The Rechargery opens tomorrow in Westminster, at 6260 Westminster Blvd, just off the 405 freeway. Look for the big sign. For the first weeks, you can charge at a promotional rate of $0.20/kWh. Afterwards, IONNA will charge its standard rate of $0.39/kWh.

Perhaps more importantly than a latest charger opening, though, is IONNA’s announcement today that Teslas can now use its network with Plug & Charge functionality (well, technically Autocharge, which is basically the same thing).

Recent findings suggest that what this means is that you can link your car and credit card ahead of time (via the Presto charging app), then simply plug in at any IONNA station and start charging, without having to tap or swipe or open an app. This is similar to the experience Teslas have always had on Superchargers, so should be familiar to Tesla owners.

The functionality is rolled out across all of IONNA’s network, starting today. So you should be able to test it out on your Tesla vehicle. IONNA already supports Plug & Charge for BMW, GM, Hyundai, Kia, Mercedes-Benz, Toyota, Rivian, Ford, Porsche and Volvo EVs.

Industry observers note that further, IONNA states support is “coming soon” for Stellantis EVs (Jeep, Dodge, Ram, Fiat), stating that those cars will be able to Plug & Charge on its network in December. It now supports Autocharge for about two thirds of the EVs on American roads.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • When this GM EV1 project car finally drove into daylight, it was 30 years to the day from when the very first EV1 rolled off the assembly line.
  • Watching V212 roll out of the garage was a moment 12 months in the making.
  • According to recent reports, caruso brought the V212 to Kettering University in Flint, Michigan, to celebrate its finished restoration, where he interviewed some of the people who worked on the original EV1 project.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When this GM EV1 project car finally drove into daylight, it was 30 years to the day from when the very first EV1 rolled off the assembly line. Nicknamed V212, after a part of its VIN that proves it's the 212th EV1 ever made, the plucky little electric hatchback is finally back on the road after a nearly 20 year hiatus, much of that spent in a Georgia impound lot. Rebuilding this three-decade-old EV was no easy task but with a bunch of help, even some from GM itself, the EV1 is alive once again.

Watching V212 roll out of the garage was a moment 12 months in the making. It all started at the Georgia impound lot, where the V212 sold for $104,000, despite being sun-faded, tired, and legally abandoned. The forgotten EV1 was bought by Apple employee Billy Caruso, who owns several early EVs, and the restoration was done by Caruso, Jared Pink from The Questionable Garage, and GM. Engineers and designers from GM who worked on the EV1 back in the day helped support the project and offered up parts from an old donor car.

According to recent reports, caruso brought the V212 to Kettering University in Flint, Michigan, to celebrate its finished restoration, where he interviewed some of the people who worked on the original EV1 project. And the passion and love that everyone who worked on the EV1 has is evident. The EV1 wasn't the most successful car GM ever made, but it was a massively key project for the future of the brand and one that made a massive impact on everyone involved.

"Honestly, I've had a lot of really good roles in my career," said Linda Ludek Brouns, former propulsion system engineer for EV1. "Hands-down favorite was my time working on EV1.

Caruso's project wasn't an easy one. V212 received a full strip-down to bare metal, its interior was completely removed, and even its glass came out. Its interior was refreshed, it received all newly introduced glass, and it was painted. It was a painstaking process but V212 now is about as fresh as it was in 1996.

In a recent development, bringing cars back to life is always heartwarming for us gearheads. But when that car is as rare and special as the EV1, it's so much more meaningful. The story is made even more special by Caruso being able to show it off to the people who designed, engineered, and built it. Thankfully, due to Caruso being willing to spend six figures on a project car, The Questionable Garage's dedication to the project, and GM's help, a piece of automotive history lives on instead of wasting away in the Georgia sun.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Video leaked in August highlighted the main character speeding by traffic cameras.
  • If you keep driving along the route where you alerted the cameras, the authorities will keep following you, just like in real life.

Industry observers note that if you thought you were going to escape the nightmare of our growing surveillance state by blowing off some steam in the sprawling world of "Grand Theft Auto 6" this week, I've got some bad news for you. Just like if you actually boosted a car on the streets of Miami, there are cameras and police databases to keep an eye on your every simulated illegal movement. Just having the fastest car on the map isn't going to cut it anymore. To successfully make Vice City their domain, players are going to have to think strategically.

Video leaked in August highlighted the main character speeding by traffic cameras. The heads-up display showed three connected dots to indicate the car was being targeted by a license plate scanning camera, according to PCGamer. Passing those cameras will alert the cops to your location, and the you'll immediately enter a red zone where the authorities are hunting for you.

If you keep driving along the route where you alerted the cameras, the authorities will keep following you, just like in real life. The best way to escape those searching eyes of the flock-like cameras (and therefore the cops) is to low-key drive out of the red zone, just like in previous iterations of the game. Cops will also respond in more force (aka you'll gain more stars) if they know for sure your character is the perp they're seeking. Changing clothes, cars and weapons after a heist can help you give the cops the slip, states Techradar.

It has been revealed that it's fair to say that the Jalopnik crew is wildly excited to tear through Vice City on some vaguely familiar but, for licensing purposes, completely unique high-end sports cars and grow our own individual empires. Whatever keeps us inside and away from the watchful eye of our tech overlords. When you emerge from your self-imposed video game exile, rubbing your eyes in the full light of day, just know you didn't waste a week of your life. You've actually just helped make real world driving safer.

  • Nothing man-made has ever gone that far, but of course you knew that, since the Voyager 1 has been the farthest man-made object in the universe since 1998.
  • Recent findings suggest that though it will forever traverse the void of space at 38,000 mph, Voyager 1 will not live for much longer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It seems like only yesterday (well, July) I was writing about signals from the Voyager 1 probe taking 23 hours to reach Earth. But as it has for decades, and will continue to do for millennia, the probe that first launched in 1977 has made more progress on its journey beyond our solar system and out to the stars. On November 18, at 5:16:07 a.m. EST, a signal from Voyager 1 will take a full 24 hours to reach Earth — because it will be exactly one light-day from our planet. This is just under 16.1 billion miles, the distance that a photon of light traverses in a single day. If you point a flashlight (a really, really bright one) at just the right patch of sky on November 17, its light will reach Voyager 1 right as it's crossing that point. (At least from the Voyager 1's relative frame of reference; from your reference frame, it will take... well, ask Einstein.).

Nothing man-made has ever gone that far, but of course you knew that, since the Voyager 1 has been the farthest man-made object in the universe since 1998. There is nothing in the works that will overtake it, either. On its journey, it took close-up photographs and readings of Jupiter and Saturn, discovering new rings and moons on both worlds. With its mission completed, it was then granted a second one: to study the edge of the heliosphere, the "wall of fire" that marks the boundary of the Sun's magnetic influence. After itself passing through the heliosphere in 2012, Voyager 1 has been studying the outer cosmos, sending information that takes ever longer to reach home.

Recent findings suggest that though it will forever traverse the void of space at 38,000 mph, Voyager 1 will not live for much longer. Its plutonium power generator is slowly decaying away, now producing just 230 watts – less than half of what it had when it was young and vital. These days, only its magnetometer and plasma wave subsystem are still performing science research. NASA does hope to keep Voyager 1 and its 68 KB of computer memory powered up enough to make it to its 50th birthday next year, though, and there are some celebrations planned.

Eventually, however, Voyager 1 will send no signals at all. Its plutonium generator will run out completely in the next 10 or 15 years, per Science News. Even before that, it's very likely that its reaction wheels (which keep it pointed in the right direction) will fail soon. Once that happens, it will drift into a spin, meaning its communications dish will not stay pointed at Earth. It will not speak to us, and we cannot tell it how to keep doing science.

The object itself will persist, reaching ever farther out towards the stars, our planet's ambassador to anyone who might receive it. Physically attached to it is the famous golden record, which carries audio and images of a greeting from our species as well as a celestial map that points the way to Earth. So even if Voyager 1 speaks no longer, it will have a lot to say if anyone out there ever finds it, however many light-days or light-years away they are.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that one can’t overstate how vital the Marshall plant is for Ford.
  • It has an annual production capacity of 20 gigawatt-hours and can manufacture 50 battery packs every hour.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that ford just reached a critical milestone in the development of its Fathom electric truck. The company has started manufacturing low-cost lithium-iron-phosphate (LFP) battery packs at its $3 billion BlueOval Battery Park Michigan, located a couple hours west of Detroit, in Marshall, MI. These are production-grade LFP batteries which will first be used in Fathom prototypes before full-scale manufacturing begins next year.

It has been revealed that one can’t overstate how vital the Marshall plant is for Ford. It’s the first plant in the U.S. to manufacture LFP batteries for mainstream consumer vehicle use domestically. LG Energy Solution also produces LFP batteries in the U.S.—supplying to GM and Tesla—but they’re dedicated to stationary energy storage systems. Ford’s 2 million-square-foot facility is dedicated to automotive LFP batteries.

It has an annual production capacity of 20 gigawatt-hours and can manufacture 50 battery packs every hour. It’s a vertically integrated plant, where materials like raw lithium and iron-phosphate powder go in one end, and fully assembled, ready-to-install battery packs come out the other. All anode and cathode production, as well as major production processes in between, happen inside the plant.

Alan Clarke, the vice president of advanced development projects at Ford, said the manufacturer is moving fast to bring the Fathom to the market. In a relatively short time period, he claimed, Ford had developed the all-newly introduced Universal EV Platform that will underpin its future EVs, an all-new production system at the Louisville Assembly Plant, and domestic LFP battery production.

“Not having a team that existed to have a battery factory, a unicasting factory, an entirely new most automated vehicle production facility that Ford's ever produced in less than five years would be I think faster than China speed,” Clarke stated during a media roundtable at the BlueOval Battery Park Michigan on Tuesday.

Clarke previously worked at Tesla for 12 years, helping create the Model S, followed by development work for the Model X, Model Y, Model 3, and Cybertruck.

BlueOval Battery Park Michigan drone photo.

Recent findings suggest that I toured Ford’s LFP plant this week, and I think it’s one of the most advanced, highly-automated battery facilities in the U.S. Michigan, America’s automotive manufacturing hub for a century, certainly hasn’t seen anything like it in its history.

Sources indicate that part of the reason why the facility is so cutting-edge comes from Ford’s LFP licensing deal with China’s CATL, the world’s largest and the most advanced battery maker. The U.S. has been lagging behind China and Europe in the battery technology race. Ford is now bringing that technical know-how back to the U.S. even if that means licensing technology from CATL.

It has been revealed that more importantly, Ford officials said the new plant is fully compliant with the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) rules. Raw materials used to make batteries here do not come from what the U.S. government designates as Foreign Entities of Concern (FEOC). Even though the technology is from CATL, the critical materials aren’t sourced from U.S. FEOCs such as China, Russia and North Korea. (China controls the vast majority of the global critical materials supply chain.).

Final inspection of the Ford Fathom's LFP prismatic cells.

The plant is fully owned and operated by Ford, but CATL engineers helped the firm set up thousands of incredibly complex production tools. They’re also helping train workers to operate high-tech equipment and install tight quality control systems to help Ford deliver the affordable EV that it has long promised. The prismatic LFP cell itself is unique to Ford and not something that exists in CATL’s global portfolio.

Recent findings suggest that meng Wang, the director and chief engineer of battery cell industrialization at Ford summed up the CATL partnership well. “To shorten our time to market, we decided to learn from the best,” Wang mentioned. “Throughout the process, CATL passed on critical knowledge to Ford, including the equipment functions, manufacturing process, and also quality controls.”.

Preorders for the Ford Fathom will begin early 2027 and production and deliveries are expected to begin by the end of next year.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that as the franchise has evolved over the decades, Grand Theft Auto became a series of sweeping crime epics rather than merely an excuse to boost cars. GTA 6 looks to be putting just a little more emphasis on the "auto" part of its name, bringing Rockstar's signature attention to detail and simulation to all the latest cars it has. Case in point: in a game full of heists, shootouts, and epic romance, you will now also have to fill up your car when it runs out of gas. Excitement! Adventure! Joking aside, this new twist may actually add just a little more spice to your bank robbing. Because sometimes, things are most interesting when they're going wrong.

It has been revealed that mechanically, this ought to be less of a burden than driving an actual car, even if it's more than the "infinite gas" of GTA games past. While you're navigating all those cool cars around Vice City's streets, you'll have a fuel gauge slowly ticking down; the game will also tell you once you've hit half a tank and again once it's nearly empty. Nearby gas stations are marked on your compass, so they're easy to find and plentiful across definitely-not-Miami. When it's time to gas up (or charge up, since electric cars are very much a part of the experience), just roll up to a station and hit RT/R2. That will trigger a 10-second cutscene. So, yes, fueling up is part of GTA 6, but also, no, you do not have to sit there and manually pump it yourself.

It has been revealed that you might wonder why Rockstar bothered adding this in at all. The point of the game is to have fun, right? A world where you can break all the rules, and the rules (including, you know, physics) are pretty loose anyway. In this case, the key seems to be about giving those crimes a little extra oomph. If you hijack a car, the game is modeling how much gas/charge it has at the time. So once you're getting chased by the police, it's now possible that your newly acquired engine is about to sputter out on you. Then you'll have to leap out of it and try to dodge the cops on foot. Okay, now that is a bit interesting!

Recent findings suggest that in terms of how often you'll be filling up, well, that depends on how much of your time in-game you spend driving. Kotaku ran a few tests and found that vehicles took 18 to 29 minutes to go from full to empty; that can vary based on the car and how you're driving. Keep in mind that crossing Vice City in its entirety only takes about 15 minutes, so this represents quite a lot of driving before you need to stop for gas. And remember, there are lots of stations, and it's just a 10-second cutscene before you're on the road again. Not too bad.

Recent findings suggest that just in case that's still too much burden for you, there's another option. The in-game Scooter Bros app lets you to call in a vehicle that you actually own (you don't have to steal absolutely everything), so you can swap from one ride to the other. And hey: As extra as this part of the simulation might seem, at least it's not so detailed that you'll ever put gas into a diesel engine.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Toyota is recalling 19,000 electric C-HR SUVs globally, with about 10,000 affected in the US.
  • In September, Toyota issued a safety recall involving certain model-year 2026 C-HR electric SUVs in North America.
  • Toyota initially noted about 10,000 models were involved, but later confirmed the number was 8,521 in a letter to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Toyota is recalling 19,000 electric C-HR SUVs globally, with about 10,000 affected in the US.

In September, Toyota issued a safety recall involving certain model-year 2026 C-HR electric SUVs in North America.

Toyota initially noted about 10,000 models were involved, but later confirmed the number was 8,521 in a letter to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA).

According to Germany’s federal motor authority, Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt (KBA), the recall has now expanded to 19,000 C-HR vehicles globally. In Germany, the recall impacts 1,096 vehicles and is still under investigation by the KBA.

The issue stems from faulty software programming in the EV-ECU. While it’s intended to limit the battery’s charge level, the software can cause it to overcharge under certain conditions.

Toyota noted the problem occurs if the battery is already at a high state of charge and the driver continues using the regenerative braking system.

When this happens, warning lights and a sound will alert the driver, and the electric drive system can shut down, causing the vehicle to lose power while driving.

Following an internal investigation, Toyota remarked in the NHTSA report that the matter was caused by incorrect software that disrupted the charging-limit function, allowing the battery to overcharge while driving.

The Toyota C-HR vehicles included in the recall were produced between June 17, 2025, and July 9, 2026.

In Europe and other overseas markets, Toyota sells the C-HR EV as the C-HR+ to distinguish it from the gas- or hybrid-powered version.

Owners of affected vehicles in North America can take them to a Toyota dealership, where the battery ECU software will be updated free of charge.

Industry observers note that toyota mailed owner notification letters out on October 18, 2026. Owners can contact Toyota’s customer service at 1-800-331-4331. The recall number is 26TA17.

Other than saying the EV-ECU is being reprogrammed, Toyota has not yet announced next steps for owners of affected vehicles outside North America. The KBA reference number is 17116R.

Check back for more details. The recall only affects the 2026 C-HR. The 2027 Toyota C-HR is also now on sale.

In a recent development, there may be a few people about to take some time off work for "personal reasons," by which they mean "to play Grand Theft Auto 6." It turns out, 43 of those people will be soldiers in the U.S. Army's 9th Brigade Engineer Battalion at Fort Stewart, Georgia. While they are being offered four days off from their duties to, you know, defend the nation, this isn't just something the Army is handing out for free. In order to grab this special leave to virtually boost cars, the soldiers also have to reenlist. Would anybody take that deal? One long weekend of gaming in exchange for years of life as a soldier? It turns out, dozens of people stated, "Hooah!".

Sources indicate that looking a little closer, this might be a little less unbelievable than it sounds. As Task & Purpose reports, getting to play GTA for a few days wasn't a deciding factor in whether or not to stay in the Army. Most of these soldiers were already considering reenlistment anyway, so they took the deal as an extra bonus. The bigger idea here was less about incentivizing people to stick with the unit — things like a $60,000 re-signing bonus will handle that — and more about showing that the command sees and appreciates the hobbies of its troops. "We understand you; go ahead and play with your virtual cars," that sort of thing. Is that the kind of leadership that will keep you from entering civilian life? For 43 people, apparently the answer is yes.

In a recent development, this offer was only made to 130 people, so about one-third of those eligible took it. That looks like a relatively successful effort, especially for something that only costs the Army four days of leave per participant. Could Rockstar Games be the answer to the Army's recruitment woes?

Look, not everything the mighty United States military tries is going to be flashy, or even something you'd assume even matters all that much. Just last month, the Army tested a bold upcoming technology that would put its helicopters at a level beyond any other force on Earth: in-flight peeing. Have you ever considered this before? No! When you stop and think about it, does it actually make sense? It does, in fact. So maybe a few "we get you" signals from command might just foster a tighter relationship between officer and enlisted. And that, as any veteran will tell you, really, truly does matter.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kia has cemented itself as one of the world’s premier electric vehicle manufacturers. And it's spent longer experimenting with EVs than you probably think. This week, Kia marked 40 years since its first EV hit the road. It reveals just how far the automaker—and the EV industry—has come.

According to recent reports, kia’s first EV introduced in 1986 and was very vital for several reasons. It was based on a van called the Besta. This was Kia’s first van developed in-house, replacing the Mazda-based Bongo van that it was making before.

Industry observers note that ahead of the 1986 Asian Games, Kia decided to develop a marathon broadcast vehicle that could keep pace with runners and house timekeeping and camera equipment—all while not disturbing runners with exhaust fumes. So the automaker ripped out the Besta's 2.0-liter diesel engine and replaced it with an electric motor and 35 kilowatt-hours worth of lead-acid batteries.

The range wasn’t great, but it was enough to cover the whole 26.2-mile marathon on one charge. Hyundai says it had around 75 miles of range and a top speed of 56 mph. It made another appearance at the 1998 Seoul Olympics.

Most importantly, Kia notes the Besta EV was South Korea’s first-ever EV. The brand would go on to continue developing EV prototypes like the 1991 Sonata EV and 1992 Excel. In 1993, the Pride EV hatchback became Korea’s first EV certified for commercial sale, although it didn't get a full production run. This car, which you may have known in gas form as the Ford Festiva, had an (estimated) 17.4 kWh battery and solar panels that Kia remarked were good for almost ten miles of additional range.

The Kia Ray was the brand's first production electric vehicle, launching in 2011 with 86 miles of range.

Eventually, Kia made its first true production model, the Ray EV, in 2011. It had a 16.4 kWh battery pack and 86 miles of range. Three years later in 2014, the Soul EV came to market, bringing a Kia EV to the U.S. for the first time. And things really took off from there.

There’s only a four-year gap between the 93-mile Soul EV and the 238-mile Niro EV. In a relatively short amount of time, Kia’s EVs went from being useful as a second car to having enough range to be a sole vehicle. Today the company has a deep and competitive line of EV models, including the EV2, EV3, EV4, EV5, EV6 and EV9—although we are missing some of those options in the U.S.

And forty years after the Besta, Kia is back to making electric vans. The PV5 went on sale last year, offering several battery options and a range of up to 258 miles WLTP. Sales are off to a promising start; Kia claims it sold some 57,000 of them in the van's first 14 months on the market.

  • About three years ago, Reddit user u/madasafish2010, whom the BBC claims is Lukas Holmes, posted in r/GTA6 about his 2009 Ford Crown Victoria Police Interceptor being used for "extensive audio recording" by an unknown entity in 2021.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar Games may not have created or used any licensed vehicles in Grand Theft Auto 6, but it's possible it's using recordings from real-life cars to make the gameplay sound realistic. The sounds of the older Crown Victoria police cars chasing you in one of your many heists may have been inspired by a young U.K. owner's police car.

About three years ago, Reddit user u/madasafish2010, whom the BBC claims is Lukas Holmes, posted in r/GTA6 about his 2009 Ford Crown Victoria Police Interceptor being used for "extensive audio recording" by an unknown entity in 2021. He remarked he was told that the work was for a Scotland-based organization's high-profile video game. His car was invited to the Millbrook Proving Ground in Bedfordshire, England, where Holmes said it was put through its paces by Niki Faulkner, a stunt driver known for his work in "Gran Turismo," "Rush," and "Mission: Impossible — Fallout." In a video about the car, he added that it was covered in microphones and used for several hours that day.

Holmes wrote that he was never told Rockstar had anything to do with the work — he just started putting the pieces together. "It was some firm that was contracted to do the work for game developers, which kinda adds up when you see Rockstar have hired other smaller companies to do their dirty work before." He added, "Niki Faulkner working on a 'high-profile video game project' only led me to one conclusion out of common sense: Rockstar North [is] based in Edinburgh, conveniently the same small country me and my car are both in ... It'd work out cheaper for them to work with local cars than to go abroad and do it.".

Owning an old Crown Vic police car was a childhood dream, Holmes told the BBC. He purchased it from the Warminster Township Police Department in Pennsylvania, then imported it to England. He raised money to fund repairs and upkeep via his company Rent-A-Vic, which rented the car to media. It took six weeks of work to bring it back to its former glory, and hours of personal time to recreate the accurate department graphics.

It has been revealed that holmes noted that his car's old-school 4.6-liter V8 has a distinct sound, as do many features like the doors closing, the warning chimes, and the 4R75E transmission. Those sounds, he predicted, would likely be used for the game's police cruiser or taxi.

Industry observers note that his dream may have become a reality. In the "Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look" trailer, at 18:24, Lucia (one of the game's two playable protagonists) is speeding in a Dodge Charger look-alike. While speeding, an excited influencer is lying in the open trunk, recording the adventure. On her tail, just barely in frame, is a police car with the Vice Beach Police Department. You have to be quick to catch it, as only the front half of the car appears behind the chat function. Some of the siren audio sounds similar to Holmes' car, as shared in his video.

Sources indicate that while the vehicle in this portion of the extended trailer more closely resembled a Dodge Charger Pursuit, other sections of the trailer, like 18:09, show police cars resembling Ford's Crown Vic. In the GTA universe, the Vapid Stainier model primarily bases its design on the Crown Vic. Just note that if you get behind the wheel of a Stainier for a prolonged joyride, you'll have to fuel up virtually after driving at what we assume will be the proper speed limit.

#433. US battery storage just topped 200 GWh – here’s where it is

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (751 w)

US battery storage just topped 200 GWh – here’s where it is

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (751 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The US has installed more than 200 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of battery storage, with nearly 50 GWh coming online in the first nine months of 2026 alone.
  • Recent findings suggest that the US added 48.3 GWh of battery storage through September, up 20% from the same stretch last year, according to the latest report from the Solar Energy Industries Association (SEIA) and Benchmark Mineral Intelligence.
  • It has been revealed that texas added 12.3 GWh of grid-scale batteries through September, more than any other state.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The US has installed more than 200 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of battery storage, with nearly 50 GWh coming online in the first nine months of 2026 alone.

Recent findings suggest that the US added 48.3 GWh of battery storage through September, up 20% from the same stretch last year, according to the latest report from the Solar Energy Industries Association (SEIA) and Benchmark Mineral Intelligence. Q3 was a little slower: The US installed 14.3 GWh in those three months, down 1% year over year.

It has been revealed that texas added 12.3 GWh of grid-scale batteries through September, more than any other state. Arizona came in second at 7.7 GWh, followed by California at 6.8 GWh. And 11 states had already broken their annual storage installation records with three months to go – Colorado, Massachusetts, Utah, Michigan, Georgia, Mississippi, Virginia, Iowa, Montana, Alabama, and Illinois.

According to recent reports, utility-scale batteries did most of the work in Q3, accounting for 12.2 GWh of newly introduced capacity. Businesses and industrial sites added another 1.3 GWh, and residential added 746 megawatt-hours (MWh). That was the best Q3 yet for home batteries, though installs through September were still down 12% year over year. Some homeowners moved up their installations last year before the federal residential clean energy tax credit ended.

“States are moving from targets to centralized procurements,” stated Pete Tillotson, a senior analyst at Benchmark. In September, Newly introduced York awarded contracts for eight battery projects that can deliver about 950 megawatts (MW) combined. SEIA and Benchmark now expect 708 GWh of storage across the grid, homes, and businesses by 2030, up 3.7% from their previous forecast.

In a recent development, the US can also make more battery cells here. A Tennessee factory opened in July and an Indiana factory opened in October, bringing US cell manufacturing capacity to 92.4 GWh, up 50%.

Solar and batteries helped bring down average summer wholesale power prices by 42% in Texas’s ERCOT market and 51% in California’s CAISO market between 2021 and 2026, according to SEIA’s inflation-adjusted analysis. When batteries had power to spare during peak hours, grid operators could call on expensive power plants less often.

You wouldn’t know it from looking at the total on residential electric bills. The cost of generating power for households fell in both markets, but the cost of delivering it to homes rose. Overall, residential bills rose 22% at the two California utilities SEIA examined and 3% across its Texas utility sample, driven by higher transmission and distribution costs. California is upgrading its grid to reduce the risk of wildfires. Texas is expanding its grid for rising demand and make it more resilient to storms.

Industry observers note that more than 300 solar and battery storage companies in the US wrote to Congress last week asking it to pass the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act. SEIA CEO Tim Pawlenty indicates the permitting bill would help get projects built faster and ease pressure on power prices. However, many Democrats feel this bill falls short. The Senate voted 70–27 on Monday to end debate on the amendment containing the bill’s text, moving it closer to a final vote.

#432. Europe’s Inland Barges Need a Cargo Proposal Before an Electric Fleet Plan

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (984 w)
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cleantechnica

Europe’s Inland Barges Need a Cargo Proposal Before an Electric Fleet Plan

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (984 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that coal throughput at Rotterdam rose 15.3% in the first nine months of 2026.
  • Sources indicate that rotterdam’s latest throughput release explains the coal rebound through recovering coking-coal movements, expensive natural gas and power-market conditions.
  • Sources indicate that the Central Commission for the Navigation of the Rhine counted 6,224 dry-cargo vessels in Rhine countries in 2025, down from 6,410 in 2023.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that coal throughput at Rotterdam rose 15.3% in the first nine months of 2026. Crude oil and petroleum-product volumes also increased. An inland vessel operator looking only at this year’s cargo market could see decades of work ahead. But an engine, battery conversion or replacement vessel bought now may still be operating in 2050, when the mix of cargo travelling through European ports and rivers will be different.

Sources indicate that rotterdam’s latest throughput release explains the coal rebound through recovering coking-coal movements, expensive natural gas and power-market conditions. Meanwhile, Eurostat reports that EU inland-waterway freight fell 3% in 2025 to 118 billion tonne-kilometres. Coal and crude-petroleum freight rose that year, while agricultural freight contracted. These changes are reshaping the services that ports, vessel owners and customers need to buy.

Sources indicate that the Central Commission for the Navigation of the Rhine counted 6,224 dry-cargo vessels in Rhine countries in 2025, down from 6,410 in 2023. Smaller vessels account for much of the decline. Tankers moved the other way, rising from 1,400 in 2022 to 1,477 in 2025. The numbers describe a fleet already adapting to changing cargo and operating economics.

Industry observers note that my TFIE Strategy Briefing on the inland barges Europe will need in 2050 uses a cargo-first model to work from the freight task to the future electric fleet. The underlying 98-page Inland Freight Electrification report is available to read.

Sources indicate that A vessel owner has two connected capital decisions. The first is whether the freight service will still have customers through the useful life of the asset. The second is which propulsion and charging system can perform that service economically. Starting with equipment and then finding a market for it risks spending scarce investment capital on the wrong vessels.

I modelled a large European industrial port corridor from a 2025-style baseline to 2050. The central scenario assumes bulk cargo falls from 57.8 million tonnes to 34.4 million tonnes, a decline of about 40%. Wet bulk accounts for much of the loss, falling from 34.5 million to 15.0 million tonnes. Dry bulk declines from 23.3 million to 19.4 million tonnes. The model is a transparent scenario for investment decisions across this type of corridor, rather than a forecast of Rotterdam’s exact future cargo volumes.

The largest change is fossil-linked cargo. Fossil fuels and refinery streams fall from 19.0 million tonnes to 1.5 million tonnes, while coal and other solid fossil fuels fall from 2.5 million tonnes to zero. Combined, those reductions account for about 20 million tonnes of the scenario’s 23.4-million-tonne net decline. Any operator whose principal customers depend on moving coal or petroleum faces a different replacement decision from one carrying grain, construction minerals, chemicals or scrap.

Industry observers note that steel illustrates what cargo substitution means. The model reduces imported iron ore and other virgin iron units from 4.5 million tonnes to 3.0 million tonnes, while scrap and circular feedstocks rise from 1.8 million to 3.5 million tonnes. The industrial function continues as the materials moving to and from factories change. Existing barges and terminals may find new work, although parcel sizes, loading systems and routes will also change.

Biofuel feedstocks create a second trap. In the central scenario those movements peak near 5 million tonnes in 2030 before falling to 1.5 million tonnes in 2050. A temporary freight boom can support profitable operations without supporting a upcoming vessel or terminal investment with a thirty-year life. The durability of the contract matters as much as the volume carried this year.

It has been revealed that cargo tonnage alone cannot size an electric fleet. The model translates commodities into powered vessel-equivalents using parcel sizes, routes, loaded calls and productivity. It starts with around 1,150 powered vessel-equivalents and ends with 664, a reduction of 42%. Dry cargo falls 17% in tonnes but 43% in powered vessel-equivalents because the modelled freight service changes. The starting 1,150 powered equivalents represent about 1,234 physical hulls after counting unpowered barges moved by pushers. Battery conversion decisions concern powered units; terminal and cargo-handling decisions also concern the additional hulls.

It has been revealed that that distinction is particularly notable for pushed formations. A pusher provides propulsion for several cargo barges. Converting one powered unit does not necessarily mean replacing every physical hull. Counting all hulls as propulsion conversions would inflate the equipment and financing requirement.

Low Rhine water levels bring a different constraint into the same calculation. A barge can remain on the register yet carry less freight per journey when draught is restricted. Cargo owners may have to buy more voyages, use different hulls or shift some freight to rail and road. Route depth, seasonal load factors and terminal access belong in the service model alongside cargo demand.

According to recent reports, ports should begin with a living cargo and route register showing which freight is declining, which remains, and which changes its material inputs. Vessel owners can connect that register to remaining hull life, annual utilization, cargo contracts and the cost of electric conversion. Utilities and terminal operators can then size grid connections, charging facilities and battery-container pools against vessels that will run on bankable routes. Infrastructure developed around dependable freight customers has a stronger prospect of earning a return.

Europe has good reasons to electrify established, high-utilization inland freight now. Battery-powered vessels are already serving container and bulk routes. The commercial opportunity is to invest in routes with surviving customers and electrify the services they will continue to buy. Expanding an electric fleet before measuring that freight task puts the order of decisions backward.

Industry observers note that the complete TFIE Strategy Briefing works through the cargo substitutions, fleet denominator and investment decisions. The open Inland Freight Electrification report includes route-energy modelling, battery-pool sizing, terminal requirements and programme economics. TFIE Strategy also undertakes scoped corridor and fleet assessments for ports, operators and cargo owners.
